title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Long Review, forgive me!

Wow, ok guys, I got to tell ya…..this Acer Predator XB323U GP monitor is really really good. Let me give you a little back story really fast though. I am replacing my Acer Predator XB271HU and I am currently testing a Dell S2721DGF at the same time I am testing this XB323U. So I am comparing two really good monitors right now, 1 will stay on my desk and the other goes back. These are my initial thoughts after owning this monitor for the past 36-48 hours.

So the XB323U arrived, in a massive box by the way. The box was like 35 pounds or something. The monitor is fully assembled when you take it out and that probably explains why it is so big. It comes with a headset holder that you attach to the stand and it comes with a DP 1.4 cable, HDMI 2.0 cable, and a USB cable so you can use the USB ports on the monitor. I personally bought an extra longer DP 1.4 cable so I could better cable manage around my desk. So that is what comes in the box…..no assembly required. The stand is made of metal, not plastic, and feels very durable. The entire build quality of the monitor definitely feels premium, kind of like buying a really nice Lexus over a base model Honda to compare.

So here are my initial impressions upon turning it on. Forgive me because I will make a few comparisons to the Dell S2721DGF throughout this review which I am sure most won’t mind because that is a kick ass monitor too. This is a AHVA IPS panel on the XB323U and it is really good. The Dell has a LG nano IPS panel in it. The Dell has an extremely vibrant color set out of box and I recommend anyone buying one to use custom color settings. My XB323U came and appears to be calibrated out of box. On standard color settings the only thing I did was up the brightness to around 75 and contrast to around 50. I like to use the Eizo Monitor Testing suite to see how well my monitors perform for initial testing. I had a perfect pattern tests as lines were straight and colors looked great and faded perfectly. I had zero dead or stuck pixels and one of the most important things is I had virtually zero back light bleed with my panel minus an almost unnoticeable area on the bottom right side of the screen. I am nit picking here because unless you are in a pitch black room with an all black screen it’s virtually unnoticeable. IPS glow is minimal but only noticeable if the entire screen is black. To be honest, I was extremely surprised at how well the black contrasts on this monitor are. For IPS, at least on this one I got, the blacks are super on this monitor…..bravo Acer! I’ve had my fair share of TN and IPS monitors and this is the best one I’ve seen to date. Keep in mind it varies from monitor to monitor. One important thing for me is black and color uniformity throughout the panel and how well the panel is evenly lit across. Without having actual test equipment, I perceive no lighter or darker areas on the monitor and colors seem fantastic. This seems to be one of the best uniformed panels I have owned to date. Also my gamma seemed to be on point at 2.2 using the Eizo Monitor Testing suite.

For productivity work using Excel, Word, CAD, Chrome and Edge, etc. the size of this screen is very enjoyable and easy on the eyes. Text in all font sizes is clear and sharp. I like the extra size and real estate to have multiple windows open and toggle between them side by side. On smaller monitors you can’t really do this effectively. This is much more enjoyable to work on than the Dell S2721DGF. Also, watching videos on YouTube and Netflix was enjoyable and should provide a great experience for anyone wanting to play media on this monitor.

For gaming, this is where the monitor really shines. My gaming rig uses a 8700k OC’ed to 4.8ghz on all cores, 32gb 3200mhz Corsair Vengeance memory, and a EVGA RTX 2080 XC Ultra. I spent a solid 8 hours last night putting this monitor through a variety of games I play a lot such as CS:GO, PUBG, Battlefield 5, Apex, Rogue Company, PGA Tour 2k21, Diablo 3, and League of Legends. I am an avid CSGO and PUBG player so those stick out the most to me during my testing. For me, I think Acer did right on this panel to cap it at 170hz as it provides buttery smooth game play, with GSYNC on and off. If you play with GSYNC “off” screen tearing is not even noticeable especially you are pushing 160fps+ however if you are averaging lower fps like around 100 you should be using GSYNC to maximize your experience with this monitor. I can’t perceive any additional input lag while using GSYNC but I tend to keep it off anyways because I can drive high frame rates. Out of box this monitor is configured to run 170hz automatically as long as you use a display port 1.4 cable. The monitor comes with 3 overdrive settings: off, normal, extreme. Normal overdrive is the best setting I found and ghosting is non-existent. The input lag and responsiveness is seriously excellent and will make serious gamers very happy. On a side note, there is a setting in the OSD called “Ultra Low Latency”…..DO NOT turn this off. It is on by default and is important to keep your input lag low…..I am not sure why anyone would turn it off anyways…..just don’t touch it! In regards to HDR content, I am a little new to the HDR world. I did fire up Battlefield 5 and turn HDR on it things seemed a little more vibrant and bright. HDR is something I am going to have to play with a little more to see how to fully utilize it so my initial thoughts here are just that. I will add more to this post later about HDR. Just know that with HDR turned off the maximum brightness is 400nits and with HDR enabled it is 600nits and there is some sort of zone dimming on the edges otherwise this could not have achieved Vesa’s HDR600 rating. This is a really fast IPS panel and is definitely a step up in speed compared to my old Acer Predator XB271HU (still a great monitor btw!). Comparing my gaming experience to the Dell S2721DGF I am testing is so similar. I can honestly say that the Dell using the LG nano IPS technology feels really great for FPS gaming on a 27inch but there is something about the immersive experience I get on this XB323U that makes it stand out above the Dell. I think it’s the size, brightness, and how well the black contrast and uniformity is that makes it seem better. I will say though, the Dell has a little better black equalizer option in the OSD.

If you are worried about the 93 PPI on a 32inch 1440p monitor, don’t worry. I sit a few feet away and can not see any pixels. If you sit with your face in the monitor you will see pixels and probably destroy your eyes so make sure you sit 3-4 feet away or more and you’ll notice the image and pixel density is really perfect. It compliments the resolution and size of the monitor very well. So for those PPI nerds out there, chill out…..this monitor looks fabulous. Also, I know people are itching to get 240hz 1440p panels but please be realistic in what you ask for. Most gamers are not going to be able to take advantage of true 240hz 1440p gaming and secondly to pay additional money for an almost unnoticeable difference is a throw away unless you are in the top %0.5 of gamers who need every last millisecond to compete on a professional stage. I am a monitor snob and I have bought and returned a few 1080p 240hz panels over the past year and the feel between 170hz and 240hz is almost imperceivable. This is the XB323U GP and the XB323U GX 240hz is supposed to come out after the 1st of the year….bare in mind that the GX is supposed to only be a HDR400 monitor too so there is a trade off depending on what you seek.

In conclusion, the Acer Predator XB323U is really a fantastic monitor. I was worried about buying this at first because this is a brand new release and no reviews were anywhere to be found. So I took a leap of faith and I am really glad I did. I will be returning the Dell S2721DGF to BestBuy and this XB323U will remain on my desk as my new primary monitor. I am excited to see TFTCentral or RTINGS.com do a review on this to see how they rate it. I know it’s going to be good. I think this monitor will compete very well against the Samsung 32inch G7 without all the issues the G7 has. If anyone is on the fence in regards to this monitor, don’t be. It is a premium monitor and it’s price seems justified to me. This will suite you well in productivity, media, and gaming…..even those serious gamers.

UPDATE: I have had more time to play around with HDR on this monitor and I must say watching HDR content on this monitor is extremely enjoyable. It's so immersive and the colors are so life like....you almost feel like you could reach out and touch what ever you are viewing. The zone dimming is fantastic on this panel and blacks look very good and mesh well with vibrant colors. Everything is so sharp and crisp. In regards to HDR gaming, after playing around with HDR settings in some games, I don't think HDR gaming is fully there yet in video games. I messed around with BF5, Shadow of Tomb Raider, and No Man's Sky........HDR just didn't seem to pop for me in those games. Was there improvement, yes but not like the experience you get while watching HDR videos and movies. It is very important to know that you need to turn HDR "on" in the screen menu before turning on HDR on in the windows Display Settings......otherwise you won't experience HDR to its fullest. I've set up a profile for gaming with HDR turned off and a profile for HDR that I swap between on the monitor. I love it, seriously love this monitor.

16 JAN 2020 UPDATE: Almost 3 months in using this monitor and I love it. I love it so much that I am tempted to pick up a 2nd one and go dual display. Colors are great, response times are great, gaming on it feels fantastic. This a great all around monitor and should fill the 1440p big screen gap for a lot of folks out there.

text: I've had this monitor a little over a month now and I like it, but in some ways it can be annoying. Unboxing and setting up the monitor was a breeze. The only problems I seem to have are firmware related which I believe could be fixed with a firmware update. This monitor at times has issues detecting the input of my PC. This leads me to either unplugging the monitor or the Displayport cable and plugging it back in, which can be annoying as it occurs more often than usual. The screen has gone dark once or twice during gameplay, and the instruction manual that comes with this thing is bare bones and will leave you trying to figure settings and features out. The 1ms VRB setting can only be used if you have your refresh/ frame rate locked at 120hz/fps on your pc or if you play a ps5 game that can run 120hz. This is information the manual should explain. I find HDR 400 to be gimmicky and I rather turn it off. If you can find how to calibrate the picture to your liking it's actually a pretty decent monitor. HDMI 2.0 can accept a 4k signal from ps5, which I believe downscales to 1440p rather than being native 4k, but only at 60fps. I like the build in aim feature as it gives you precise crosshairs on the screen, I find this useful for high fps games like apex legends. I've noticed after a month slight led bleed in the left bottom corner of screen which is more noticeable dure night game sessions, but is tolerable as you only notice it when the screen goes dark. Other than a few cons this monitor can handle the performance of a high end pc, and it actually looks really good and is as smooth as butter during gameplay. Like I said I believe the issues I do have with this thing can be fixed via firmware update. I hope this review helps and Acer gives this boarderlining amazing monitor the support it needs!

I like getting good value for my money without spending on features with diminishing returns, and I feel this monitor fits the bill nicely. title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
My monitor setup in my home office is… well… complicated. I regularly switch between a MacBook Pro for home and personal projects and a high-performance Windows laptop for work. Add to that two 32” curved monitors that I use for both setups — but in different orientations — and my desk becomes a constant exercise in cable management, arm gymnastics, and fighting off my chronic MDS (Messy Desk Syndrome… it’s real, trust me).

For home use, both monitors stay in landscape. For work, I need one in landscape for code and one in portrait for reference material. The monitors’ stock stands can rotate, but the clearance is so low that they just barely skim above the desk clutter… and if you have MDS, that never ends well. Half the time I skip switching orientations even though it would help me work significantly better.
So when I saw this dual monitor arm system on Vine, I hit “Request Product” instantly. Maybe — just maybe — this would solve my monitor dance.

Well… it didn’t. But not for the reason you might think.

Setup & First Impressions
I checked my monitor specs first. The system supports 4.4 to 19.8 lbs, and my monitors weigh 10.58 lbs each without their stands — perfect. If your monitor is too light, it will float upward. Too heavy and it will sag. Also check your VESA pattern: 75×75 mm or 100×100 mm are supported.

When the stand arrived, the quality looked fantastic. Packaging was clean, parts organized, and they include a generous assortment of mounting screws for different monitor types.
Setup is very straightforward. The main decision is between:

* C-Clamp mount
* Drill-Through mount

Since I was testing on a side desk first — not the final location — I used the C-Clamp.
One thing they could improve: The small plastic desktop-protecting pucks are too hard and don’t grip the desk well. They also fall out constantly while you’re trying to position the clamp. Annoying, but not a deal-breaker.

I grabbed an older 27” test monitor from the basement, removed the stand, attached the VESA plate, and mounted it. It worked great. The arm motion is smooth, articulation is generous, and the tension adjustments behave as expected.

Everything was going perfectly… until my youngest son walked downstairs.

The Plot Twist
He saw the stand. His eyes lit up. He claimed it like a crow spotting a shiny object.

There was no convincing him otherwise. Promises of chores were made. Christmas lists were mysteriously revised. And suddenly I was helping him mount his monitor to the other arm.

He’s thrilled — the extra desk space is huge for him. (Will he use that space for homework? Let’s not delude ourselves. But the potential is there.)

My oldest saw it next and went straight to Amazon to buy his own. So now both kids have monitor arms…. and my own desk problem still exists. Looks like I’ll be buying another one.

Bottom Line
✅ Excellent build quality and packaging
✅ Handles full-size 32” monitors with ease
✅ Smooth articulation and easy positioning
✅ Includes screws for a wide range of VESA setups
✅The cable management on each arm is perfectly placed and works great
✅ Great price for what you get
✘ Hard plastic pucks fall out and don’t grip the desk well
✘ Now I have to buy another one because my kid stole it

If you need a dual monitor arm system, this is a great value and performs extremely well — assuming you can keep it from being “borrowed” by anyone else in the house.

text:
Item: AOPEN by Acer 32S1U PRO 31.5" 4K UHD Touch Rollable Smart Device | Android System | Google Play Store Support | MPP 2.0 Pen Support | 8M Wireless Camera | WiFi 6 | Bluetooth | Height/Swivel/Tilt/Pivot

This rolling tablet has a beautiful high-quality screen, it's versatile for many uses, moves easily, and is simple to use! I've waited to review this item to test it out and leave an informed review thoroughly. I'm an Apple user, so this is the first time I've used an Android device, so there was a slight learning curve, but this tablet is easy to use! I've only had one issue with it (in the last 6 weeks), which was at the 2-week mark of using it. The touchscreen wasn't responding to my touch and it was only responding to the volume and power buttons. After multiple attempts, I could force it off and restart it, and my issue was resolved.

The packaging for this product was excellent and the assembly was straightforward for one person to accomplish. Other than one screw being an annoyance to get in, it all went smoothly and quickly. The materials of this product are high quality and the brushed gold looks lux and blends nicely into your decor at home or in an office. The audio is crisp, clear, and able to get loud enough to project across the room. The base rolls smoothly and easily, and the screen can be moved into a landscape or portrait mode, making it easier to move through doorways and small spaces, and for varied uses. The screen can also be tilted up and down, as well as side to side. The camera has a magnetic component and can attach to multiple spots on the perimeter of the tablet, which is ideal if you want to flip the screen from portrait to landscape mode for zoom calls. And you can leave the camera off of it altogether.

The three buttons at the bottom of the screen are for volume and power and there is a touchscreen to navigate the apps. I find this tablet is great for streaming movies, live TV, zoom calls, checking emails, and surfing the web. Even with an Apple product, I was able to move my information over to this tablet for a quick startup and had my passwords and other information saved upon initiating the start-up. This tablet can be used for creating artwork as well, with a special MPP pen, which is not included. I haven't tried this option out yet, but think it would be great for artists, to use in meetings, brainstorming, study sessions, etc.

The information states that this tablet has a 4-hour run time but I suspect it may be a little less. I will try to update this later with that info. But the charging cord easily plugs into the base at the back, with a long cord. There is a light on the front of the base that indicates if the battery has a good charge and when it starts running low it turns red. The screen will also prompt you to plug in the cord.

This tablet also alerts you when you receive email messages and other notifications. You can turn them off or turn the volume up or down on these alerts.

I’ve found that this makes a great additional tablet and TV, which could be moved around the house to various rooms with ease. I’m interested in seeing if there is an optional remote to purchase to make streaming easier. It can be annoying to have to use the touchscreen or buttons to adjust the video playback and volume at times.

TLDR: Overall, this is an excellent product, and I'm pleased with how easy it is to use! This tablet has many functions/uses and would be excellent to use at home or in an office setting. I love that it can easily be moved from room to room, which increases its usefulness and accessibility. The picture quality of the screen and audio are crisp, clean, and of excellent quality. I highly recommend this product and believe it would be great for non-Android users as well.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text: I am coming from an IPS Predator panel. I didn't chose to buy this screen because of picture quality but because I wanted a higher resolution. Coming from 1080P, so this one was within my price range. Also wanted HDR whereas my last panel didn't support it. I've been using this one for a day and a half and I must say it's eye opening what I was missing out on. Also a lot of misconception regarding miniled panels. The picture quality is just as good and even BETTER than the predator it replaced. The 180hz refresh rate is less than the 240hz it replaced but I can't notice any difference, no input lag or ghosting at all. Smooth and clear. The brightness of this screen with HDR enabled is INSANE, you just don't know what you are missing until you have tried true HDR. The colors in SDR isn't as good as my IPS panel but once you turn on HDR the colors are better than my predator monitor and insanely bright. If you find it too bright you can turn it down to whatever level pleases you. The 1152 lighting zones give this miniled a HUGE bonus to darks and bright images. Meaning very deep blacks and bright brights! I have a fairly new OLED TV and I can't see any difference between the two technologies. The color options in HDR is greyed out so you can't adjust it but I can see why this is the case. It doesn't need any adjustment at all... The colors are fantastic in HDR. To keep all the goodness of HDR not just while gaming you can turn it on for windows operating system as well. I turned it on for everything. I really did not understand what a huge difference HDR makes. Ran some identifying software Aida, and says it's putting out over 1500 knits brightness in HDR. Games just look 100% better with HDR it's no contest. I'll never go back to non HDR viewing. 1440P is the sweet spot for gaming and navigating windows. Even when HDR is on you can adjust the brightness to your liking. You will have to make certain adjustments for this panel in terms of contrast but I made all the changes within the first few minutes. Also has game setting for boosting smoothness but it's refresh rate of 180 hz is more than good enough by itself. Well done KTC for getting consumers what they want. No frills monitor and great quality!

This miniLED monitor is phenomenal, and gives you a lot of functionality and picture quality for a relatively low price. If you use your PC for a mix of work and gaming, this is a great alternative to OLED options that can be at risk of burn in. The HDR looks great, the dual mode resolution switch works very well and saves all of your options, and the usb-c 60w port is very useful for plugging in laptops, and charging phones. Some have said that the local dimming could be better, but I think that is only a problem when looking at the screen from an angle. When facing the screen forward, the local dimming does a great job of keeping the dark colors dark.

I've seen some complaints of dead pixels, and bad packaging, but mine was packaged very well, and as of now, there are no dead pixels or black spots that I can see. Everything looks and runs well right out of the box, and I don't have any complaints.

Are there better options out there? Of course! But for the price, its really hard to beat what this display has to offer, especially if you are upgrading from a 1080p setup. This manages to do so much, and I think the pros heavily outweigh the cons.

Pros:

Smooth and responsive gaming performance

Sharp image quality

Cons:

Dead pixel appeared within days

Small dim area on screen

Quality control could be better

Overall:
For $165, the monitor delivers great specs and performance, but quality control is a concern. If you’re on a budget and can tolerate minor defects, it’s still a solid deal. If not, you may want to invest in a higher-quality option.

After a month of use I am ready to give it a simple review. As a lifelong gamer with eyes sensitive to ghosting I'm usually a harsh critic when it comes to most screens.

So when I say that this discount off-brand monitor blew my mind please know that this isn't an exaggeration. Yes I may have gotten lucky, but regardless the model sent to me is surpassing every expectation.

PROS:

Speed - The screen seems most comfortable at either 120hz or 200hz. It felt a little off at 165 but that may be my own eyes.

Setting overdrive to Off or Normal seems to give the best results along with the high refresh.

Color - HDR is pretty damn good on this thing. Not as good as some expensive oleds would be but still surprisingly good. Otherwise set the screen to Movie for the brightest and most vivid SDR colors.

Cons:

MPRT felt weird to me. Reverse ghosting weird. So just leave that off.

Wasn't too big a fan of the VRR but it definitely works fine. Just kinda mutes the colors a notch and feels like strobbing but that is probably just my eyes. My friends and wife have all said it looks great with VRR to them. I just keep it set to 200hz

Conclusion: For the money you cant beat this screen. Ive been using it with games both on my PC and also streaming with GeForce Now (which seems to lock to 120hz on it) and it works great either way.

*** UPDATE 12/23/21 ***
This update is to correct the top negative review titled "It's not IPS and it's not 75hz". I don't know where this person gets their information from, but the claim that you "cannot have both 1080 lines of resolution and 75hz at the same time" is completely false and untrue. And I'm a 20+ year I.T. tech. I've just attached a picture showing this monitor running at 75Hz in Linux. I've also had it working just fine at 75Hz in Windows as well. Now while you can't visually tell much (probably none) difference between 60Hz and 75Hz like you can going from 60Hz to 120Hz, 75Hz is still better than 60Hz. And this monitor has been working fine at 75Hz since the first day I've owned it. If that reviewer's statement were true, we wouldn't be able to run monitors at 100Hz, 120Hz, 144Hz, 240Hz, etc. The ONLY way this monitor would NOT run at 75Hz is if one's video card or video card drivers do not support 75Hz. Mine does and that's why I posted the picture of the monitor working at 75Hz. That reviewer's card or drivers likely did not support 75Hz, so the option wouldn't be there.

It sucks that Amazon took away the ability to comment on someone's review. Otherwise this would have been corrected long ago, and probably wouldn't be the top negative review that everyone sees first. It really bugs me when someone leaves a negative review with such completely inaccurate or false information, and then it goes unchecked and others say the review is helpful.

Having said that, I've had zero issues with this monitor. It's crisp, clear, colorful. And has been running flawless. Still 5/5. Definitely worth the money.

If you're looking for a first gaming monitor that won't break the bank, or are on a tight budget and want a monitor that looks great or even an inexpensive second monitor, this is about the best you can get. And I've done my research. Go for it!

Not only that, but if you hit if you hit the trigger too far left or right it instead turns up and down the volume from it. Just be ready to be up close and personal with it to fix the display settings.

I did have one more issue with it, but it was more of a problem with Amazon itself and not the monitor. I only mention this to bring awareness to potential buyers. On the day I purchased the monitor, it was listed as $240. But literally the day after I purchased it, I went to reread its specs and found that now it was listed at only $200. And even when checking the official Koorui website, the monitor is listed as $200 as well, although it is sold out on the website and only accessible on Amazon. Be cautious to check the pricing so you don't end up having to pay more than it is truly valued at. It might not seem like a super big deal to you, but as a college student struggling at times to make ends meet, it is a big deal to me.

Overall I am heavily satisfied with this monitor and if I ever want to upgrade or replace my other monitors, I will highly look into purchasing another product from this company!

The paper guide included with the AOC monitor does NOT describe how how to use these buttons. The HOMEWORX manual omits fully describing how to prepare for, record, and playback TV programs on a USB flash drive. If you are computer savvy, formatting, recording, playback and deletion of TV programs is easy to figure out. If not savvy, you may need to ask HOMEWORX for help.

The AOC monitor is very easy to set up. You just need to insert the neck at the bottom of the screen into the base. The screen can be tilted from 20° up to -5° down. You plug in your 1 or 2 HDMI cables from the HOMEWORX tuner and your computer, the power cord, and your speaker or earphone 3.5mm connector cable, and you're done! The HDMI button under the bottom screen edge allows you to easily switch between the tuner and your computer. Audio is automatically switched between devices with the HDMI button. On Windows 10, a 24B2H2 Intel(R) Display Audio interface is automatically installed by the AOC monitor and becomes the Default Playback Device. I have an audio cable running from my computer to my speakers in addition to the HDMI cable. If needed, I can switch the Default Playback Device back to Realtek High Definition Audio to enable me to record audio using Audacity software, which I use to record stock market Earnings Webcasts. (Note: Audacity requires a wire connection between the Realtek audio output and input to enable recording audio off the Internet.) The AOC display itself is excellent, strong clean colors and high definition. The screen is matted, NOT glossy as incorrectly listed by Amazon.

The HOMEWORX tuner has a handy easy to use large remote control along with manual control bottons on the tuner itself. In addition to the HDMI port, it also has RCA jacks and can act as a HDTV converter box for an old analog TV or as audio output for a stereo amplifier. It has a USB-A port for a USB flash drive or other form of storage drive. When not turned on, the HOMEWORX digital display acts as a clock showing the time of day. Signal reception by the HOMEWORX is excellent. This has the best reception of any HDTV tuner I've used so far, and I receive stations I could not receive before so long as the weather and temperature inversions permit.

It takes the weight off my actual laptop hinges and keeps everything totally stable. I never felt like the screen was going to tip backward.

Instant "Wake" Time Setup was intuitive—I was up and running in minutes via USB-C and HDMI. One specific technical win that I really appreciated: when I wake my computer from sleep, these monitors turn on at the same moment as my main display. There is no lag and no "handshake" delay.

For business tasks, text clarity is the most important thing to me. At 1920 x 1080 for each monitor, the text is crisp and easy to read. I run Windows scaling at 125%, and there is zero blurriness. The brightness is consistent across the panel, and the viewing angles hold up really well, which is critical when you have screens angled on the sides.

The S8 Pro has genuinely improved my multitasking capabilities. It gives me that "command center" feel without being too bulky to move around. If you are looking to expand your workspace for productivity, I think this is a competent choice.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
The build quality is very nice. Very solid feeling and no concerns with holding a big monitor like the X34. The Value is great.

A couple of design criticisms:
(1) Like most arms, this one has a sloppy tilt feature with 1 screw that you have to tighten exactly for it to hold and hope that it droops to the right tilt angle. While the weight is a few lbs under the rated 19lbs max, it still was a trick. You can see from the pictures its had curved washers which provide point contact, probably for ease of adjustability for lighter monitors. To get this monitor to stay, I switched those out for regular washers for full surface contact (more friction). It took a day or two and a few re-positionings to finally get the washers to wear in and hold. It's been holding for a few months now even after moving the monitor to different positions so I don't think it will be a problem again. Basically once you get it settled in, it works great.

(2) The top and bottom arms are not the same length. The reason this is a problem is that at first I had mounted the arm in the center (like previous arms) but that means that the monitor can not be centered to the base unless the arm is rotated most of it's length back towards the wall (which is around a foot or so). It's kind of hard to explain, but trust me it's a problem. The solution is that you must install the arm to one side about 3in (check before you install), so that the monitor will sit centered without needing to be extended forward or back.

(3) The plastic covers for the cable management are a bit flimsy and the bottom one slides off while the top one clips on. I confused it and accidentally busted the bottom one. Luckily I only planned to use the top.

But overall I'm a big fan to have a clean desk with this arm.

This is fantastic. This is one of those things that you think is an unecessary and expensive luxury, until you have one. I got a Humanscale monitor arm for free at work and after just a week I liked it so much I went out and bought one for home.

Compared to a monitor stand, this arm is drastically more adjustable. I have my computer desk in my bedroom. I can move the monitor to the rear of the desk for work, move it closer to my face for gaming, or swing it off the side of the desk and lay on my bed to watch movies.

A monitor arm saves a lot of desk space. This frees up space for my large mouse pad and keyboard. It also gives a more minimal and clean aesthetic.

I previously had the humanscale monitor arm rated for 16 lbs, which is hardly more than my 14 lb monitor. This meant that regardless of how I adjusted the springs, the monitor would droop 2 inches below maximum height. Not with this arm. It holds at the peak height without dropping. The monitor tilt and rotate action seems to have improved in the M8 over the older enterprise M2 I first bought.

The swivel action at the base and connection between the 2 arm-pieces is incredibly smooth and low-friction. The black matte finish and base are sleek and match the frame of my monitor.

The only concern with this is there isn't a built-in way to keep cables from slipping 3-6 inches down and off the bottom. This resulted in the DisplayPort plug getting yanked hard to the side as I rotated the top of the arm and almost broke it. After I used the velcro ties to keep it up, that hasn't happened again. However, I'd prefer some internal mechanism. This is a very minor quibble though and easily worked around.

This arm is worth every penny.

I purchased two of these adapter to mount Viewsonic VX2776-smhd monitors to a new Vivo dual-monitor mount. (Interestingly the two adapters together cost more than the Vivo mount they are adapting).

The adapters slid in easily and appear to provide a secure fit to the monitor, though I did not hear the 'snap' the instruction manual indicated I would hear on either adapter install.

When I attached the first monitor adapter to the Vivo mount, the monitor fell off. The issue appears to be the screws fit snugly on the adapter plate, though are smaller than the Vivo mount plate, so when screwing in the provided screws it felt like there was a secure threading, but they were only threading the adapter. (I tried the alternate holes in the Vivo mount plates after that and had the same issue). A run to the hardware store to pick-up eight (four for each monitor adapter) 8-32 coarse wing nuts solved the problem. They really should have included the nuts with the adapter.

Understandably, with the adapter now in place, I found the monitors would easily tilt forward (as the Viewsonic monitors mount at the bottom, making the setup top-heavy), not a knock on the adapter - as is meant to be the case, tightening the y-axis tension bolt on the mount solved for that. Just need to have that allen wrench handy when mounting.

Putting aside the setup hiccups, the adapter appears to working on its first day of use.

While we don't currently use the arm to actively move the screen around (though we may transition to that at some point, it isn't as important for a TV as compared to a monitor primarily used with a computer), what I love about this arm is that it has so many degrees of freedom that it was super easy for me to install it onto the TV while the TV was already attached to its stand, and on a desk that isn't very deep (so we couldn't have the arm sticking out too far where it would not attach properly over the top of the desk where the TV is situated, i.e., we don't have the flexibility to stretch the arm out past the edge of the desk since the TV was on the stand which is resting on the desk). There was absolutely no problem with bending the arm in a way that it situated the mounting plate exactly where I needed it in order to attach it to the TV, very easily.

This is also a possible way to transition to using only the arm without the stand, now that it is attached to the arm, I can increase the tension, maybe place something soft under the TV just in case, and then lift it a bit and remove the stand, while already attached to the arm. It would be a bit difficult to attach such a large screen to an arm safely without some kind of support, but this method would allow me to do it myself without much risk.

Before purchasing I carefully reviewed the weight limit, the various joints and how they moved, and the various lengths of movement along each direction. I knew this arm would be perfect for what I needed based on all that, and many of the others on the market did not appear meet my needs (or it wasn't clear), and it worked out perfectly, as expected.

I did need to get an adaptor to fit this to the TVs mount, it works perfectly but I guess it would be nice if the arm came with one since many larger screens that it supports are likely to have larger mount dimensions.

The one thing I cannot really comment on, since I don't use it this way, is the ease of continued day-to-day regular movement of the screen, and how easy it is to adjust the tension appropriately for that usage, though from what I have seen, I doubt it would be an issue.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I got two Gladiator Joe VESA bracket adapters (model #GJ0A0055) for use with two Acer G227HQL Abi 21.5" monitors. The overall quality is good and the fit is excellent. I would buy them again even knowing what I do now (see below).

I was happy to find out that there are adapters made to convert my Acer monitors to a VESA mount - I thought I was going to have to fabricate something myself. Now, for most people this mount will be just fine and I could easily give 5 stars. For the rest, I'll show the things I felt were shortcomings or disappointments even though some may consider it nit-picking. That's why I removed one star.

1. The top image for this model adapter on Amazon shows the monitor mount welded to the BOTTOM of the back plate. The adapters I received had the monitor mount welded to the MIDDLE of the back plate. Although the forth image down shows a monitor attached to the mount welded to the middle of the plate. I do not see any reason to have this mount welded to the middle since the mount is just as strong in the bottom position, and both HDMI and VGA connectors on the back of the monitor will not be affected. Some of their other adapters have it mounted to the bottom where it should be. Looks like someone did not update the image when a change was made at the factory.

With the monitor mount welded to the middle of the VESA plate, 1.5" of the back plate will be visible below the monitor. The left monitor will be mounted to the wall above my desk, so this negative is only cosmetic. But the right monitor not only has 1.5" of the back plate visible below the monitor, it also takes up space on my desk since this monitor is situated 5" above my desk.

I corrected this by cutting 1.5" off the bottom of the back plate so the monitor mount is now flush with the back plate. Grinding the welds off and welding the monitor mount to the bottom would also have been an option. I drilled two holes at the bottom of the back plate, next to the monitor mount since I removed the bottom portion. This modification removes the full VESA mount, but it doesn't matter for me since I have them installed on custom mounts.

2. The monitor mount is 2" deep to the back plate. That does not leave much room for a straight HDMI connector. It will fit, but a sharp 90° bend has to be made right at the connector. My thin (0.215") cables are easy to connect, but my thick (0.375") cables are a little more difficult, but will certainly fit. A much cleaner installation is to use a left (90°) or right (270°) connector. When an HDMI socket is orientated so the shorter length is on the bottom then looking at a socket this way, a "left" cable will go to the left (90°). A "right" will be 270°. Search Amazon "left HDMI cable" or "right HDMI cable" for their selections. This is not to be confused with an HDMI right-angle adapter for "bottom" being referred to as 90°, and "top" is referred to as 270°. A "top" would exit to the top of a monitor in this case, a "bottom" would not fit since the monitor mount is in the way.

3. One adapter had cold welds. This means that during welding, not enough amperage was used to create enough heat to melt the metal, which results in poor penetration. A weaker joint is the result although it is still strong enough in this application. My other adapter had good welds.

4. The paint was not dry (hard) on both adapters. Upon receipt (both packed VERY well), there was a strong petroleum smell and slightly tacky - not to the point where fingerprints would be left, but it was VERY easy to scrape the paint off with somewhat light fingernail pressure, leaving bare metal. If an adapter was left on paper, it would stick to it. No primer was used. After two weeks there was not much change so I stripped the paint so I could repaint them (this time with primer).

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
VIVO has updated their stands and the new ones are clear improvements of the previous one.

Having used the one monitor as well as the two monitor stands before the update, the changes are mostly great:

The base has been made wider and as such also lighter and thinner, making it far easier to handle. The rod in the middle has also gone from having three screws screwed into the base, to being a big screw in itself that you screw into the base. Which feels a lot nicer and sturdier.

However with three 24" monitors mounted, it feels like it's on the verge of tipping forward when I try to adjust anything on rod.

The new cable management is a huge improvement to previous versions which just was a clip that mounted into the hole in the arm where you'd run your cables through. Now it's a separate, albeit plastic, holder that hangs from the arm. The rod part has gone from having a hole where you stuck a holder in, which inevitably broke or just popped open and let the cables loose, to a solid plastic clip with a clipping mechanism for the cables. It also now includes two holders for two hex-keys that are used to adjust the mount. Oddly enough the package had three hex-keys off different sizes that were all used: One for the rod to be tightened into place and two for the arms adjustments. So I'm not sure what I'm supposed to do with the third key.

Now the arms have gotten updated and most bolts have seen the removal of bottom nuts that you had to hold in place to steady things.

Except for the swivel part of the monitor holder, which instead of the previous quite excellent thumb grip that allowed for tool-less adjustment as well as a free swivel, has been replaced with a nut and bolt, which makes it rather uncomfortable to adjust since you now need a wrench to stop it from wobbling about.

The last issue is the rod part of the arms. both the arms mount and the middle mounts adjustment bolt face the monitors, so while the middle monitor is on, it's hard to adjust both the arms as well as the middle monitors height, making it a bit of a hassle for the first time setup to get things right.

Further it's also, as with most mounts, VIVO or not, a bit hard to adjust three screens without any type of marker on the adjustment arms to tell what angles you're in, leaving you with a lot of fidgeting to get it to feel right with the rotation, tilt and angles. This isn't something that's specific to VIVO products, but considering how well made their products are at this point, it feels worthwhile to point it out in hopes that they'll work on the quality of life parts next.

Beyond that, it feel a lost sturdier while also lighter, the new arms feel safe and bulky, which is a great improvement from previous bone style arms.

In summary, despite the list of issues pointed out, none of them are even close to dealbreaking, and VIVO maintains some of the best mounting equipment out there for some of the best prices. I'm yet to be disappointed or even considering returning any of their products.

Mount-It offers a a dual-arm model, which I returned because that setup requires that each arm share a base, which greatly limits how you can adjust and configure the monitors. If you have two monitors, I would get two arms.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I finally decided on this arm after seeing negative reviews at the top of every monitor arm/stand I could find. I figured going with a metal one was a better bet to reduce wobble and better secure my somewhat expensive Zowie monitor. I could not be happier with my purchase, it cleared up A TON of room on my desk compared to the fat stand that came with my monitor. I don't really move my monitor at all, but I was able to place it exactly where I want it and just leave it there. It was fairly straight forward to set up even coming from someone who has no prior experience with anything like this. The only thing worth mentioning is that the part that controls the up/down tilt had to be tightened pretty tight until it would hold. I wasn't sure I was doing it right because it didn't seem to move much, but it definitely does tighten.

I believe almost all the bad reviews must've just been people who got a bad unit which can be easily returned or replaced through Amazon's generous return policy. It is not fair at all to give the company no chance to fix any issues which many reviewers seemed to do. Something I can say is the arm is fairly hard to move when the arm is not anchored to anything, which is probably the cause for some of the complaints about it being too stiff. It's likely that some units are actually too tight, but for my unit, once I attached it to my desk, it's fine. It's still firm, but very easily movable with just one hand. The upper arm moves by just pulling on the monitor, but the lower one I would adjust by hand if you ever need to move it. Similarly, some reviewers just didn't read any instructions and don't understand that you have to tighten a bolt to increase the pressure of the pneumonic arm. It is not supposed to hold up the monitor out of the box, you are supposed to adjust it to suit your monitor's weight. It's not extremely obvious which way is loosening or tightening, but worst case you can just try both until it works.

One thing to note is that you will need probably about an inch of clearance behind your desk, so your desk cannot be pushed flush with a wall if you are attaching this to the back. It was very easy for me to just move my desk a tiny bit forward to get around that. Just make sure you've considered that before buying in case you're unable to move your desk to accommodate. Other than that, my desk is slightly curved in the back but it still clamps on very sturdy and I have absolutely no worry that it won't hold.

Overall this is a very good product and I will definitely be buying another if I decide to get another monitor. If you're on the fence because of some bad reviews like I was, I am confident you will not regret buying this.

The VIV0 102-0 dual monitor stand is a decent buy for its price. It supports dual clamp/grommet which provides a secure installation as opposed to single clamp/grommet arms. The arms are made up metal and feel sturdy.
They also look good. I bought it to support 2 monitors and free-up some desk clutter.

I have mounted it by using the grommet mount as my desk has a frame came in the way of the clamp.
Mounting the arms were easy. The instructions are precise and crisp and the arms were up and ready on my desk in about 15 mins.

I have 2 monitors.
The monitor on right is a 24" HP monitor that weighs 6 lbs. That monitor took to the arm like fish to water and I needed no specific arm or mount adjustment. Also, I can swivel, tilt or raise this monitor without any issues.

The monitor on the right is a 27" Acer monitor weighting 10lbs. I had some issues mounting that monitor.
Though the pneumatic arms hold good after a few adjustments, the monitor tilted downwards. I had to basically crank up the tilt to maximum to a point that the monitor does not tilt any more. I can still raise the arm and swivel the monitor without any issues. If I loosen the tilt bolts, the monitor just tilts face down.

I think the advertised 14lbs weight capacity is over rated. May be it can support heavier monitors with some loss in functionality.
The cable management is decent. It uses clips and they can come loose. I didnot have issues with it personally but I felt better cable clamping solution would have helped.
The arms also go up a decent height. its not an issue for me as I use these monitors while sitting. It may be of concern to people who stand and work.

The monitors also stick out a bit. Be advised that if the desk is set flush with the wall like I have, there is no way to bring both the monitors together. The only way is to set the desk far away from the wall so that the arms can extend beyond the desk.

text:
I've got an S200HQL as a little secondary monitor, and this mount works well for it. It's mostly stable, it will swivel a little bit, and the stabilizer bar does help it not wobble around as much. Due to the odd back shape of the monitor, it doesn't sit flush, but there's plenty of room to move the bar around and get a pretty stable push on it.

Now for the reason I removed 2 stars... mine did NOT come with the included spacers that it was supposed to. Mounting the S200HQL is not possible (well, at least not safely) without the spacers. The screw went in very loosely and may not have held it at all. Luckily, I was able to find a couple of washers that worked well enough. If I didn't have any, I would have had to have waited for the seller/manufacturer to [hopefully] send me some, or I would have had to go purchase some.

text:
When pulling this out of the package, the mount actually feels like quality metal. Sadly, that is where the good ends. The cons...

1. Lacking necessary pieces- I have a S220HQlL, which is a monitor guaranteed to work with this mount. attempting to mount the display as specified it is immediately apparent that the screw required to attack the stem of the monitor is not in the bag. This would require you to go to a hardware store and figure out what screw works. If that were the only problem, then i would have just done that.

2. Only use with like monitors- I bought this mount so that I could put this in my 4 monitor array (2x2). My new monitor (S220HQL) was bought to go alongside 3 of its predecessors (S211HL), which had VESA mounts built into the monitors (why did you stop that Acer). If I were able to mount this without using the monitor stem to get rid of that added height, the screen would still still a couple inches higher than the monitor next to it. You include the stem....forget about it.

3. The mounts only make sense with multiple monitors that are side by side (and the same model). If you are trying to do a 2x2 or anything that involves another row, the space between would be bezel plus the stem height. The whole point of having a VESA mount it to cleanly line up displays and most efficiently use your viewing space. this mount misses so far on that objective that it's laughable.

4. Bad hardware included. Even if you have fall within all of the contingencies that I specified for the the negatives, the screws and washers that are included are not sized properly. By that, I mean that the head of the screw and a literal hair bigger that the pass-through of the washer. If I placed a screw through a washer it would be supported. However, if tapped slightly to put the screw at an angle in comparison to the washer, the screw falls through. i would not trust that combination to mount my monitor. If you made it this far in the process and still want the mount, you will have to go to the hardware store to by washers that are a proper fit.

In conclusion. I am better off taking my stand of the manufacturer provided pedestal and allowing it to rest on my office desk while leaning against the VESA mount that it was supposed to be mounted to. having an unsecured monitor sitting on my desk is better than using this mount. I hope this helps.

title: 3.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I use this monitor as I work from home 4 days out of the week & I absolutely loved it at first but the more I used it I learned that it simply doesn’t live up to the price point. Before I dive into the cons some of the pros are that for its size it’s honestly not that heavy, it’s pretty clunky but I had no issues carrying it around by myself. The monitor slides up and down which is awesome so you can be sure whether or not your webcam is on & it’s like an added layer of privacy (the webcam is super high up so if you’re short like me your head might get cut off).

And last PRO - The monitor also comes with built in speakers, they get pretty loud & although my MacBook Air sound much better the fact this monitor even comes with speakers & a built in microphone is pretty dope! some of the expensive gaming monitors don’t even come with speakers!

Ok, now for the cons…
1. If you are saving up for a high quality, expensive monitor to last you a long while please keep your options open. If you have expendable income & this isn’t a big purchase for you then buy it but if this is possibly a big purchase I honestly wouldn’t take the chance. I was able to buy this with a work from home stipend & while I make a decent salary I would be extremely upset if I paid for this with my hard earned money.

2. I had high expectations for the picture and color quality but those expectations weren’t met, I was actually a little shocked at how bland and fuzzy the screen appears. The colors seem washed out, the best way I can think to describe it is being kind of matte and not “glossy”, the picture isn’t crispy. Even just browning the web if you look close to the screen you can see the text looks slightly fuzzy. This isn’t a big deal but again, it should be clear and crispy for $500.

3. The size is awesome for gaming, if you have a Gaming PC with a graphics card this would honestly do the job but my Truly honest opinion is if you are interested in buying this for strictly gaming I’m not sure if this will be enjoyable to truly enjoy the gaming experience. I would look for monitors specifically built for gamers.

4. IT BREAKS VERY EASILY!!!! I initially thought it was a tough monitor as I’ve taken it out of town with me, hauling it in and out of the car without issue, while it held up great in the car it didn’t stand a chance against a small light piece of plastic. A figurine I keep near my desk somehow fell against the monitor & it completely demolished the screen. Immediatley broke the screen with a 2-3inch wide black line down the screen with the right side glitching out. It gradually got worse over the next few days, at first the left hand side still worked great so I honestly didn’t mind since the screen is so incredibly large but eventually horizontal purple & green lines started popping up making it hard to read my work files.

I understand that if something it’s a monitor screen it will break but I truly was shocked at how sensitive this monitor was to barely being hit by the plastic figurine. Growing up my mom was in IT and worked on computers for a school district and my uncle built gaming PC’s so I’ve used a lot of different computer monitors both high quality and crappy - unfortunately this monitor is up there with the crappy quality ones due to the fact the entire screen went out so easily.

I truly expected higher quality and for the monitor itself to be quite durable since it’s over $500.. I’ve had run of the mill monitors that have fallen off the back of a truck & still worked perfect. Since it’s a curved monitor I’m sure that plays a part into the screen being so sensitive.

The monitor lasted roughly 6 months with no issues but I really enjoyed using it as a work monitor & I felt spoiled due to how big the monitor is. I honestly think it’s BIGGER than 32 inches, it feels more like 35-38 inches because my 27inch monitor at the office is half its size.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This HP 24mh monitor has a clear, crisp display and is the perfect size for desktop use (not too big, not too small). It accepts both HDMI and DisplayPort inputs (and even VGA for old school PCs). While Windows will select 60Hz refresh rate by default, you can go into Windows' display settings and select 75Hz refresh rate for this monitor. The 75Hz refresh rate really does help smooth out motion. You should also go into the monitor's "Image" menu setting and set Response Time to Level 3 which provides the best VSYNC performance. One of the best features that places this monitor above and beyond its price range is the 90-degree rotating screen, height adjustment, and swiveling base. The stand is rock-solid without any wobble. The speakers are just fine once you discover the menu control I explain below:

HOW TO FIX LOW VOLUME SOUND: The built-in speakers are better than some reviewers indicate. I believe most people don't discover that the monitor menu has its own volume control that's set to 50% volume by factory default. If you just connect this monitor to the PC you'll automatically get sound through the HP speakers via HDMI or DisplayPort (you only have to use the separate audio cable when using the VGA input). But no matter how high you turn up your PC volume control, you'll only get 50% volume from the monitor's speakers which is why people complain about low volume. To fix this, all you need to do is go to the "Management" tab of the monitor menu, select "Audio", and then turn up the volume control from 50 (default) to 100 and you'll find the monitor speakers are plenty loud. After that, you'll only have to use your PC volume control as normal.

This is a great quality monitor with features beyond its price range. Fantastic value, HP!

ADDITIONAL NOTE: HP sells an identical monitor to the HP 24mh under the model P24h. The only difference is that the P24h has a black plastic logo strip along the bottom instead of silver like the 24mh. Everything else is identical (specs, speakers, height adjustable stand, etc.) plus the P24h comes with both an HDMI cable and a DisplayPort cable.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This is the first time I actually did research to see which options had all the features I wanted instead of buying the flagship model in the size I wanted with specs that my gpu couldn’t even fully use.

My use case: I work at home as a software implementation consultant so typical tech stuff, productivity apps, etc. I also lightly game (Fortnite).

The OLED spoiled me for sure and I can actually tell the difference now, but based on the knowledge I gathered from a weekend of binging YouTube reviews, 4k is plenty sufficient for 32”. 240hz is nice, but I’m not very good at video games and I’m not even sure my gpu can push that out.

In the past year, I’ve gone through a 49” ultrawide Samsung G9 OLED and some unimpressive 34” ultrawide LG smart monitor. I was happy with both out of the box. The G9 ended up being excessive for me and made the room too warm because I didn’t have the proper air circulation so that meant I knew I didn’t want or need OLED.

I was also over the ultrawide and curved formats so I was deciding between a 27” and 32” flat panel. The other features that were important to me were 144hz, 4k IPS, VESA compatible, built-in speakers, and SMART just because I enjoy bundles. There are many more options available if 60hz is enough for you, but I definitely noticed the difference going from 240 to 60hz so I knew I wanted 120-144.

I love this monitor (so far) and am so glad I took the time to research. Finding all your needs in one monitor reduces the need for all the endless peripheral. I highly recommend ChatGPT and YouTube to compare your options.

The only feature missing for me is a glossy screen.

Honorable mentions: BenQ 32 (geared toward Mac),
Gigabyte 32 (value), and Dough spectrum Black 32 with Gorilla Glass (it just looks sleek).

Would recommend to a friend.

Hope this helps someone!

Also worth a mention is that this coincided with the release of the Samsung M8, which is positioned as a competitor for the Applie Studio display. I almost went with that because it is cheaper than the Omen but couldn’t get over the 60hz.

I put my wishlist into ChatGPT and asked for a comparison of prices and features. The monitors that kept coming up were the HP Omen 32x, a Gigabyte, and a BenQ. BenQ was intriguing but I’m not a Mac girly anymore so I was trying to focus on functionality for once.

text:
Love it! For those on the fence, this is an update of the 165hz version. I can't tell you the exact brightness, contrast, inputlag and response time but I can give you my opinion on it. So starting off with brightness. This monitor does get bright but in hdr it only gets close or just at 500 nits. Good enough but not hdr 600. As for input lag and response it is very very fast but only at about 140 to 180hz. At 180hz especially, it feels incredible smooth and I suspect response time and especially input lag are as low as possible. Playing marvel rivals felt very smooth. Now putting refresh to about 100 or less felt rather delayed. I suspect that input lag is higher than it should be at these frames because it felt rather delayed. My older monotor is a 240hz 1080 and it felt faster at those refresh rates.

Now for contrast, I do see a little gray but since this is va comparing it to an ips it certainly is much blacker. While its no oled or miniled I think hdr can work quite well. The specs say 4000 to 1 contrast and I think its correct. Maybe a little less or a little more but in that ballpark for sure.

Finally build quality is great but I got it mounted because it does slide easily across the desk with its original one.

Summary: A great monitor with accurate colors, great contrast, super low input lag and response time especially at 140+ refresh rate and pretty good brightness. The one downside is it is 100 bucks more than one with similar specs but it does nothing wrong so I think those 100 bucks go into the quality of the screen.

text:
I purchased this monitor to pair with a nearly 3-year-old Mac Mini and was somewhat concerned about compatibility because it is an HP product. Fortunately, there were no problems at all with it working with my Mac. I knew that this would not be the best display in the world in terms of color fidelity or flexibility, but was just looking for something very utilitarian and easy to look at for hours a day. For around $100, you can't expect the best, but I am very satisfied with the display. The controls are easy to understand so you can make adjustments to color, brightness and contrast intuitively and the widescreen very helpful in dealing with windows in browsers as well as multiple palettes in applications. It is lightweight so it is easy to move around on your desk if you need to. At 1600 x 900, it looks sharp and clear. At other resolutions (which are interpolated), it is somewhat blurry and stretched, but this is to be expected from an LCD, particularly a low end one. If you need to have clarity at other resolutions, you may want to look for something more expensive.

The only somewhat negative points are that the light weight comes with somewhat flimsy feeling construction. Unless you tend to drop your display, this shouldn't be an issue. Also, it is very stiff when trying to adjust the tilt. I initially believed it was stuck, but it was just quite tight. I was a little concerned that forcing it to move would break something, but it wasn't a problem. All in all, this is a pretty solid budget display.

text:
Cet écran est remarquable dans cette gamme de prix pour le travail images/photos/
Avec des bords fin et un aspect très sobre, cette dalle matte est clairement orienté travail fixe plutôt que jeux d'actions.
Quelques boutons sous le bord de l'écran donnent accès aux réglages et j'ai pu le faire reconnaître immédiatement autant sur PC que sur mon vieux MacBook Pro 215.
Le nombre d'entrée est correcte mais il convient d'apporter une précision quant à la fiche technique Amazon puisque l'un des 2 ports Display Port est en sortie uniquement (DP Out); le reste est classqiue : 1 DP, 1 Hdmi, 1 DVI-D, 2 USB, 1 USB-C
Comme la désolidarisation avec le pied (peu gable) se fait aisément avec un bouton, je me suis empressé de le positionner sur un bras articulé puisqu'il est compatible VESA.
Bien en face, la qualité de restitution des couleurs pour le travail photo est vraiment excellente sans aucune aberration vers les bords ou écarts de luminosité.
En vidéo, notamment dans les jeux, il faudra éviter ce qui demande un temps de réponse rapide (FPS s'abstenir, RPG welcome)
En PJ retrouvez la grille d'étalonnage fournie; je la confirmerai à l'occasion à l'aide d'une sonde.
Comme d'autres je déplore la consommation : classé B en 2019 c'est vraiment dommage et lui coûte 1 étoile sur ce seul point.
timestamp_raw: Reviewed in France on November 2, 2019

text:
Le test a été réalisé avec des jeux vidéo, des logiciels de retouches photos, de vidéos (HD, UHD et 4K) ainsi qu'avec une utilisation plus basique (Internet, fichiers divers ...)
Ecran très bien fini. Bonne qualité de matériaux. Il est sobre et beau.
Les couleurs affichées sont très belles, très proches de la réalité. C'est très agréable pour de la retouche photo ou de la PAO. Et même les vidéos sont visionnables sans se fatiguer la rétine.
En jeux vidéo, il est préférable de pouvoir avoir la tête un peu au dessus de l'écran, de façon à ce que les glandes lacrymales fassent leur travail, car le pied de l'écran est très (trop) haut et n'est pas réglable en hauteur. Mauvais point.
On appréciera le fait que le pied restera où il est sur le bureau une fois en place, que nous n'ayons plus qu'à bouger la dalle en l'inclinant (droite, gauche, vers le haut ou le bat) et même en la pivotant à 90° à l'horizontale ou à la verticale.
Les connexions au PC sont multiples, à vous de choisir selon ce que votre tour ou laptop peut accueillir. Le seul bémol est la HDMI qui est une HDMI propriétaire, encore une chance que mon PC soit un HP, lui aussi, car ils ne fournissent pas de câble HDMI standard du coup.
Avoir un écran LED qui consomme autant, ce n'est pas normal en 2019.
Et le prix, je ne suis pas si sûr qu'en 2019, la LED coûte si cher. Après, c'est HP, on n'a rien sans rien. Mais quand-même, beaucoup d'autres modèles (d'autres marques) font tout aussi bien (et peut-être mieux) pour moins cher.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I bought this monitor just before Christmas and I have been really impressed so far.

It's huge. Takes up the whole desk, in a good way. The resolution is fantastic. For computing, 1920x1200 beats HDTV (1920x1080) by a big margin. You get 10% more pixels! Those extra pixels are important, especially when so many programs have menu bars and status bars on the top and bottom.

It's really easy to have multiple windows open and have the size and resolution to work with them. To get a sense of this, imagine a normal 8.5x11 inch sheet of paper. The monitor is about two and a half pages wide, and more than a page tall.

It's super bright. At 90% brightness it's almost too bright for a room without any sunlight, but of course it can be turned down if you want.

My main concern with it was that the refresh rate isn't the fastest around, but I've played some games on it without any noticeable motion blur.

I have two computers hooked up to it through a DVI-D KVM switch, and a laptop that I sometimes hook up with a DisplayPort connector. The monitor will automatically switch to whichever signal is active, or I can switch it manually if both are active. (If one signal is active then it won't automatically switch to the other one, even if that one does also become active.) [That's the default behavior, but I think it can also be set to always prioritize one source over another.] It also has a HDMI input, which I don't use so I can't speak to. It does not have an analog VGA input.

It also functions as a powered USB hub, with two USB ports on the back of the monitor that are hard to get to (intended for semi-permanently installed items like mouse and keyboard) and two ports on the left side which are easy to access.

The only hitch I have experienced is that the monitor would not work properly with my XP machine until I downloaded a driver for the monitor and installed it. This was a little trickier than it sounds, because the driver would not install correctly by itself. I had to go in and, through trial and error, figure out exactly where to install it. Once I did that, though, it worked fine. But it works fine on my Win7 laptop even though I never installed a driver for it on there.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Pros:
Great Design, beautiful look
Cristal Clear Text and Image
Great Color richness
Great color accuracy
no eye strain
tilt adjusting
matte finish(I prefer matte to glossy)
Energy Star qualified (25W maximum)
100mm x 100mm screw-mount

Cons:
No height adjustment.
no HDMI
sub per speaker
Not very good vertical viewing angle
HP Ads is too sticky

Resolution:
For this size monitor, I think 1600*900 is the ideal size otherwise the text size (1920*1080) will appear too small.

Comparing to 2009m:
2009m is the 2009 model. it is not energy star efficient qualified. it is glossy finish. It does not have 100X100 mount. For 20$ more, I would go for 2010i.

Comparing to 2210m:
The 21.5' 2210m is 1920*1080 full HD with HDMI input and is gloss screen. First of all, 2210m is a great monitor if you like gloss screen and are used to relatively small character size. However, if I have extra cash and if I like glossy screen, I would go for a larger screen such as 2310m or 2509m since the character size is simply too small for me on 2210m than that on 2010i.

Comparing to ViewSonic's VX2250WM-LED 22-Inch
I was also able to compare it to ViewSonic VX2250WM-LED. First of all, I don't think led tech will add better display experience to a monitor but make it a lower power consumption and a lighter body. Considering the color richness and color accuracy, I would like to vote for 2010i because the color on VX2250WM-LED appears to me wash-out and a little weak. The built quality of 2010i is also better. But if you want a lighter display with a higher resolution at a reasonable price, you may want to go with VX2250WM-LED.

Comparing to Samsung 2333SW
I also own Samsung 2333SW. Even if it is full HD, the color is so weak comparing to HP 2010i. The most important thing is that I always feel eye strain on the Samsung 2333SW. I just feel so comfortable working on the HP monitor.

update (11/02/2010): Comparing to HP S2031
I made a dual setup using HP 2010i and HP S2031. I got the HP S2031 from HP for a huge discount. The HP 2010i has an overall better build quality than that of HP S2031. The display experience on two monitors are quite similar except that the text character on HP S2031 has a barely noticeable greenish cast. For under $100, I would go for HP S2031.

Character size:
The character size appears larger on this monitor than that on Samsung 2333Sw 23"(1920*1080) monitor and that on 2210m. You may like this if your eyesight is not as good as before. For 21.5" and 23" monitor, I have to adjust the text size to medium (125%) to feel all right. But on this, default 100% text size appears just perfect for me.

If you are looking for a budget monitor best used for online browsing, text editing, movie playing, and photo editing, this would be a great buy. Large screen or higher resolution is not always a better choice and it really depends on your needs. If I really want to get a full 1080P experience, I would watch the movie on my Samsung 46" HDTV. After comparing different brands and models, when I sit in front of my desk working on something, this is the most comfortable screen that I ever had. I just feel the crystal clarity at every second...

Buyer attention: removing sticker from top bezel of 2010i can be a pain since the glue residue is very strong as the other reviewers pointed out. I also observed that other HP 20** series monitors received many negative reviews only because of this. HP should take serious consideration on this. Here is a tip : "Removal of advertising sticker from top bezel of HP monitors at HP Support Forum": Check out comments section below.

About HP consumer monitor 2*** model:

Have been doing research on hp monitor for a while. I went to Costco to check also. Personally, I prefer the 'i' version to the 'm' version since I don't like the glossy finish. Even with the anti-glare coating, I still see things or myself clear on the screen. I feel eye strain too (the most important thing). I wish they had a bigger screen model. Unfortunately, they don't have the corresponding 2310i, 2510i, 2710i in US(only available in UK). They do have the 2310m, 2509m,2710m in US, but they are glossy finish. the only downside with the i version is there is no hdmi input.

Example
2509m
25 means 25"

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
As others have and will say, this is a great monitor. I bought two of these. One 2010i is cabled using DVI and the other is cabled with both DVI and VGA. Very sharp image with excellent color definition for both types of connection. I use it mainly for business apps, with the occasional bit of PC gaming and it's absolutely superb for everything I need it for.

At a price hovering around the $140 mark, this screen represents great value for money too. I replaced an HP 2009m and a ViewSonic VX710. There was nothing wrong with the 2009m (or the ViewSonic for that matter), but I hated the glossy screen finish of the 2009m. If I'd wanted a mirror, I'd have bought a mirror. The 2010i has the matte screen finish which obviously doesn't pick up room light sources and reflections like the 2009m does. Much better!

However, there are a few things about the 2010i which bug me and are worth noting.

1. The power button is located near the bottom right corner (same as the 2009m). It often needs several presses before it responds to being switched on/off. I have both my 2010i screens mounted using the "Dual LCD Monitor Stand desk clamp" (available via Tyke Supply through Amazon). They look great, but adjusting the tilt means I need to grab the lower bottom edges of the screen which, more often than not, turns the screen off. A bit annoying, but not a deal breaker.

2. When I use the Source button to switch from DVI to VGA, a "Monitor Status" box appears telling me it's scanning for input signals. I know that's what it's doing - I don't need to be told and it doesn't have to obliterate half the screen with an obvious and annoying message! Maybe you can turn that off, but I haven't found that option yet.

3. Some genius at HP decided it would be a great idea to place a long sticker along the top edge of the plastic screen surround. It's the usual stuff...HP logo, screen resolution stats, connection types, etc. All the things you already know, but OK. No big deal to just peel it off, right? Wrong! The glue HP used is so strong that it's left behind when you peel the sticker off. So far I have tried duct tape, WD-40 and Goo Gone and the glue is still there. The duct tape didn't lift any of the glue off, the WD-40 just spread the glue around and the Goo Gone didn't do anything. I'm absolutely paranoid about getting these chemicals on the LCD screen itself too. Why do we need a sticker and if we have to have one, why use the same glue they use to build roads? And yes, I did peel the sticker very carefully, but it didn't do any good. Totally asinine.

So, if you want a great LCD screen for an awesome price and a glue cleanup job that'll sap your will to live, the 2010i is for you.
