text:
As an experienced user of various monitor brands, I can confidently say that BenQ monitors excel in design and performance. Their build quality, adjustability, and display technology make them a top-tier choice for professionals and everyday users.

Build Quality & Ergonomics

One of the standout features of BenQ monitors is their robust construction. The base is exceptionally sturdy, providing excellent stability even when adjusting the monitor frequently. The stand allows for extensive ergonomic flexibility, including height adjustment, tilt, swivel, and pivot, ensuring an optimal viewing experience for various work environments.

Display Performance

BenQ’s panel technology consistently delivers superior image quality. Whether using IPS, VA, or TN panels, the screens exhibit high color accuracy, sharp contrast ratios, and wide viewing angles, making them suitable for content creation, gaming, and business applications. The factory-calibrated color accuracy in some models ensures that professionals working with photo and video editing get precise color representation.

Brightness & Eye Comfort

The brightness levels are well optimized, with high nit values that enhance visibility in different lighting conditions. More importantly, BenQ integrates eye-care technologies such as flicker-free panels and low blue light modes, reducing eye strain during extended use—an essential feature for those working long hours.

Connectivity & Additional Features

BenQ monitors also stand out in port selection, offering HDMI, DisplayPort, USB-C, and legacy VGA options, depending on the model. Some premium models include HDR support for better dynamic range and adaptive sync technologies like Free Sync/G-Sync compatibility for gaming.

Final Verdict

Overall, BenQ monitors provide an excellent balance of build quality, ergonomic flexibility, and high-end display performance. Whether for professional use, casual computing, or gaming, they deliver reliable and superior visual output while ensuring user comfort. They are highly recommended for anyone looking for a durable, high-performance display solution.

The second problem was how tinny the sound was. It, as well, was horrible. This monitor's speakers have minimal sound separation (ie. musical instruments in a song), zero bass, zero mid-range, and very tinny highs. ALL tinny highs is the result. That is the reason for the 1-star. Audio this bad absolutely ruins what would otherwise be a nice computer monitor.

Hopefully BenQ will investigate this major audio quality issue and fix it. If Dell can offer a monitor (same size) at the same price point with good sound using small internal speakers, BenQ should be able to do it as well. At least offer decent sound quality. We’re not expecting studio quality sound. There really is no excuse for speaker sound to be as horrible as this. Trust me, folks, I am not exaggerating with this review. I’m being very honest here with my review. I wasn’t expecting high-end sound. I was shocked it was this bad. I have owned quite a few computer monitors with internal speakers, with sound quality varying from maybe a 3-star to a 5-star. My 1-star for these is unfortunate but deserved. I hope BenQ fixes this issue.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I’m particular about design. It took me 5 tries to find a monitor that met my needs. Thought I’d write up a review in case it’s helpful to someone else.

No one has paid me for this review. Keep in mind I am using a monitor to extend the display of my MacBook Pro.

My needs: I am a writer and wanted to be able to have multiple pages documents open at the same time. I also do some graphic design and wanted to have true colors represented on the screen. I live in a small cabin so this monitor would also need to serve as my TV—high streaming quality and beautiful resolution is a must. They pretty much only make 4K monitors in the 27” size and those are too large for me to use as a work screen and also too large for my space. That left me trying to figure out what smaller monitor would have a high resolution--it took multiple tries. I also am sensitive to light and wanted something that wouldn’t hurt my eyes after being in front of it for long hours.

Dell 24 Plus Monitor - S2425HSM

CONS
There is no option to hook up a USB-C or thunderbolt cable on this monitor. Thus you can not charge your laptop by plugging it into the monitor.
This monitor is designed so that you plug an HDMI cable into your laptop and then into the monitor. HDMI cables are bulky and don’t bend as easily as a USB-C or Thunderbolt cable. HDMI cables do not charge your laptop. USB-C or Thunderbolt cables are more bendy and charge your laptop directly from your monitor.
You cannot have your MacBook in clamshell mode (laptop closed) without having your laptop charging cable plugged in. Thus instead of one USB-C or Thunderbolt cable you have the bulky HDMI and your laptops power cord. When I had all the cables hooked up it felt messy and it was all sort of awkwardly mashed into the desk riser I built.
The text resolution of this monitor was pretty pixilated. Downloading Better Display and creating a virtual screen helped a bit.

PROS
144Hz refresh rate
The streaming quality wasn’t as good as some of the monitors I’d try later on but it was pretty darn good! Speakers are great.
Pretty much no eye strain!
It’s so odd but I completely fell in love with this monitor despite the fact that it really didn’t meet any of my core needs. I loved the color, the sleek design and the ease of the mini joystick on the monitor itself. The menu on this monitor via the joystick was really enjoyable and adjusting the settings produced effective results (more so than the U2424HE which I’ll review next). I actually liked the menu options on this (adjusting the color, brightness, gamma, screen mode etc) better than any other monitor.
I loved the 16:9 ratio which I would return to when all was said and done.
I barely was able to return this monitor because I was weirdly attached to it. I’d say this is perfect for a high school or college student. As far as budget monitors go, this is a really great option. If it had a USB C option I doubt I would have returned it or bought a thousand other monitors trying to find the right one.

Dell UltraSharp 24" Hub Monitor - (U2424HE)
CONS
This monitor supposedly has better resolution than the Dell S2425HSM. I put them side by side and played the same show. No matter how I adjusted the settings, the U2424HE looked overly red. And the resolution wasn’t that much better, if at all. Text did appear to be slightly sharper but it wasn’t a significant difference.
Contains a USB C Port but would not allow me to put laptop into clamshell mode without having laptop power cord plugged in.
Only 60Hz refresh rate

PROS
None. I can’t recommend this for anyone.

ASUS ProArt 24” (24.1” viewable) 16:10 HDR Professional Monitor (PA248CRV)

CONS
Text still wasn’t as sharp as I’d like.
I didn’t like the screen ratio. But I didn’t know how much I would miss the 16:9 of that first Dell until I tried this one. This is more of a personal preference than a mark against the brand. It does have more vertical space if that is important to you.

PROS
It features a USB-C port (one step down from a Thunderbolt cable) that handles video, data, and charging simultaneously.
Streaming quality was decent. Better than both Dells, not as good as BenQ or Asus PA24ACRV.
Daisy chaining and comprehensive USB hub with 4 ports.
No noticeable eye strain after adjusting settings a bit.
I got very close to keeping this one but I couldn’t get over the ratio. It is a decent monitor though so I ended up giving it to a friend.

BenQ MA270U 27” 4K 3840x2160
CONS
At this point I was about at my wits end and thought that I’d have to get a 27” to get the resolution that I was after. I tried to use this as my work monitor and it was overwhelming. I know a lot of people use a 27” monitor but that was too much for me.
4K panels often require much stronger backlights to push light through those tiny pixels, which can be brutal for light-sensitive eyes in a small space. No matter what I did with the settings it was too bright. This monitor supposedly has blue light blocking technology built in. Look—if eye stain is an issue for you, what I realized is that less is more. Some of these high resolution monitors achieve true colors by using a lot of light, and no amount of filters, screen shade, night shift, blue light glasses etc, is going to help with that much light coming at you. Even when I took the opacity waaaaay down and had all the filters on I still felt like I was being radiated.
This monitor is very large and heavy. Not great for a small desk set up in a small cabin. It about crushed my desk riser.

PROS
Really beautiful colors and crisp text.
Super cool software download (from BenQ website) that allows you to adjust settings. No need for clunky buttons.
Compatibility with Apple.
I ended up giving this monitor to my partner to use as his new TV in the living room. Sitting back from it a few more feet, it’s easier to appreciate.

ASUS ProArt Display 24” (23.8 inch viewable) 1440P Professional Monitor (PA24ACRV)
This is the one I ultimately kept for myself.

CONS
My main complaint is that the physical design of the monitor feels a bit outdated. Sort of 90’s. Dell did a really great job condensing their buttons on their monitor to the one mini joystick. On the Asus monitors it’s a bunch of buttons across the bottom right side of the monitor. Feels clunky. These should be accessed through the joystick or hidden.
Speakers are pretty awful.

PROS
16:9 ratio
It has very sharp text.
The silver color of the monitor base is the same as my MacBook Pro.
USB-C Power Delivery (A step down from Thunderbolt—working great for me). I only have ONE cable plugged in to the monitor and no need for the powercord for my laptop.
Daisy Chain capability with multiple USB ports for mouse, external hard drive etc. and other types as well.
Pixel Density (123 PPI). Standard 24" monitors are usually 1080p (~93 PPI), which macOS struggles to scale, leading to "gray/blurry" text.
Much higher resolution than the Asus PA248CRV that I had tried. Text is crisp. Even crisper after implementing Better Display. Seriously try Better Display. Ask Ai how to set it up. Spending $21 for the pro version of this software can make a monitor like this feel like a much more expensive monitor because macOS assumes most of these monitors are a low-resolution screen. It doesn't use its high-quality "Retina" scaling. Using this software helps these monitors reach their potential.
This monitor has a deeper black than the Dell monitors I tried where the text appeared to be a gray. Colors are vibrant and photos are incredibly vivid.
Resolution quality is great in Adobe/Design work and during streaming. I noticed that when I’m streaming from Safari as opposed to Chrome, the quality is significantly better.

text:
Firstly, I would have to say that the ideal user for this product is someone who spends a lot of time either playing video games or doing work on a screen. I personally use this product to play xbox one, but it would also be great for everyday work or even a dual monitor setup. If you play video games casually or don't spend very much time on a computer, then this monitor might not be worth the purchase. Overall this really is a fantastic product for the price.

Now I'll talk about a few positives. The colors and picture are fantastic, and the fact that it has external speakers is a big plus because a lot of monitors don't. Next, a few small negatives. The first negative is the speakers, which was actually one of my positives as well. It's true that it is a plus that this monitor actually has speakers, however they are just a little bit quiet. If you want to use this monitor for gaming and require extremely high quality sound, these speakers might not provide the quality of sound and volume capacity that you are looking for. If you fall into this category and are purchasing this monitor, I would recommend also getting some sort of gaming headset to route your game sound to, which plenty of gamers already own anyway. Overall, I was pleasantly surprised with this monitor's impressive performance given the fact that its price is significantly lower than many other competitors or even other BenQ models. This is a high-quality monitor all-together for anyone, and for those who struggle with eye strain or dizziness from screens.

text:
I was going to buy something cheaper but I ended up paying about $700 extra and going with this because we do some gaming.

I don't use the included Android TV dongle, so this review is not relevant on that front.

This is installed in a dedicated movie room receiving a signal from an Dolby Atmos receiver. We have an Xbox, a Switch, and main TV is supplied by a Google Chromecast.

Interestingly, the Chromecast supplies a 4k signal no matter what the native quality is, so it always runs in 4k unless we are on a game.

We really love this projector, it is so bright, we run it on eco mode all the time, and it's still bright enough to watch with the limited lighting on in the room. The picture is crisp, and with the vertical adjustment, it is really easy to get installed without using Keystone which reduces performance. We have it mounted on the ceiling.

It starts up very quickly, however, with the connection it needs to make to the Chromecast, it's not really much faster than our old bulb-type projector, in the long run. It's just usable at full brightness faster. What I'm saying is, it starts up fast, but takes the same amount of time to connect.

It does occasionally lose signal, but I cannot confirm where the source of that issue is. It reconnects in 15-20 seconds. Happens every couple days or so, could be the long cables, could be a bad connection, I don't know. It's not a major issue, and hasn't happened while gaming, only movies, so it may be a 4k transmission issue.

It's very quiet. It is large for a projector in my experience, the box is about twice as large as our former projector. As for the value, I think it was worth it, I'm glad I bought it. That being said, I don't know how the other one I would have bought would have compared.

I wish there were a few more settings like our old projector, but we haven't really needed to adjust anything. Maybe it's not the most perfect real life accurate color, but it's bright and vivid and awesome for watching movies and shows. And it seems like it makes Rocket League more responsive, that may be the low latency, I don't know, I'm not an expert.

Very happy with this purchase, would buy again.

Purchased this projector 3 weeks ago and have used it a bunch over those three weeks.

The short throw was exactly what I needed for my space. I have it ceiling mounted from about 7.5' and currently have it at a 135" screen size with some zoom. Having a whole wall that is a screen is from that close is pretty awesome.

The picture looks great! It isn't the brightest projector at this price range but the short throw and LED light source was worth the trade off for me as I have a light controlled room. Can definitely still watch things on it when some lights are on but dark more cinematic scenes will suffer. I haven't really delved deep into the settings or calibration yet as it is pretty good out of the box.

I also game on it and it performs well. No noticeable input lag at all. Mind you I'm not playing competitive shooters, mainly just RPG's or casual shooters with my kids.

There is a noticeable hum when the fan is running but in ECO mode it quiets down without taking away picture quality or much brightness. During a movie or game it isn't really noticeable unless you're listening for it.

It was easy to install with an universal ceiling mount. Tricky part is getting it placed in the correct spot but that would be the case with any projector without lens shift.

I don't use the built in speakers as I have a surround system and this projector has an audio return channel which is a great feature for that. When it was first set up and I didn't have the audio cables ran yet it sounded pretty good.

I am overall very satisfied with this purchase. If you're in need of a short throw projector like this its a must buy.

I am very impressed with my benq x3000i projector. Coming from using a great TV (65 inch Sony 900f), I am impressed with how vibrant the image is, and how responsive controls are while playing games on switch, ps5 and pc. The input lag is not noticeable, whatsoever. Maybe a machine test could notice the non existent input lag, but no human ever could or they're a liar.

There is no rainbow effect for me whatsoever. Fast moving content, slow moving content, no rainbow effects.

Compared to a 1080p Chinese projector(~$400), there is no comparison. The image quality, response time, machine noise(lack thereof), and appearance of the projector helps justify the price difference.

I have not tested the sound at all, other than about 10 seconds to which I switched to digital out to my av unit.

After about 3-4 weeks of heavy use, I am more and more impressed every time I turn it on. A little bit of ambient light is defeated with a bit more brightness, and then brightness turned down a bit for evening viewing. The customization of sdr and hdr settings have been easy to use and achieve a great colour to my eyes. Wow the purples, blues, greens, reds, and yellows really pop on the screen. It took a few days to allow my eyes to adjust to the sheer volume of beauty this unit projects on to a screen.

I had high hopes for this projector, and I am happy to say my expectations have been exceeded.

Things I noticed. Stardew valley has no chop or stutter, only fluid motion when the screen scrolls, which I did not realize was achievable. Cod black ops 4 is extremely fluid and I hit my shots (offline mode) more often than not. Elden ring shadow details very clearly visible while maintaining fabulous contrast. When I use a controller to aim via joystick movement, I find I am scrolling to the target, not past the target. The input lag being so snappy allows me to be much more precise. text:
The 3550 was a 4K pixel shift projector just like this one. It was in the $1500 range. It was a lamp based unit. What this unit gives you over the 3550 is, better colors, better HDR, and better dynamic contrast. 4K movies definitely have a little bit more "pop" to them. And while projectors will never compete with OLEDS in dark scenes. The contrast in dark scenes on this is good.

There is one element where this projector is weak. And this is, if the scene is almost completely dark. As opposed to say, a night time scene but where there are neon lights or flashlights. In scenes like those, this projector looks great with the HDR bright highlights. But in almost completely dark scenes, the entire scene just looks "dim".

But that is really the only negative I can think of. I've tested the 3D, and the brightness is really good even when wearing active 3D glasses. The 3D is flawless with no ghosting, and good brightness and color. And as said before, the HDR and color is very good. Please consider trying the "AI Theater" mode. There was a scene in Dune Part 2, where I switched back and forth between my custom settings and AI mode. And suddenly the orange color of the sand just looked so beautiful and vibrant in the AI mode.

This is definitely work the price if you are new to projectors or upgrading from a cheaper BenQ model. It has almost the same throw ratio so you can put it up on the same ceiling mount you already have, if you were using a 2060, 3060, or 3550. I would consider this an "intermediate" projector. Definitely better than budget entry levels, and a nice compromise between budget or going all out on a high end.

I've been watching so many movies and appreciating them more, after I installed this.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I'd like to start by saying, ever since LG invented the wallpaper TV, I've developed loyalty, strictly on their displays for everything. They are cheaper then Samsung, yet more innovative, so, kudos. That said, if my review sounds at all biased, I'm sorry. There are no defects on the monitor I received. Ran an Ezio test and found nothing that stands out.
Something to be aware of, is that if you purchase a VESA mount, it needs to be 100x100, and even if that mount has spacers, you may need some washers to compensate for a gap. The reason for this, is to keep the back flat and uniform when installing the stand it comes with, but considering monitors these days are naturally very thin, this causes a problem by limiting the female port length for the screws needed to secure a VESA mount. In my case, 8 small washers I had left over from other projects fixed this problem. Something else worth noting is it is Nvidia G-Sync compatible (there is an attractive sticker showing this monitor is capable of it on the bottom left that I'm assuming can be removed). My Nvidia GeForce RTX 2070 Super recognized that it is a G-Sync compatible monitor, and I was able to enable G-Sync thru the Nvidia Control Panel, however, when you view settings on the monitor itself, it is called "Adaptive Sync." From what I've read, this is because they used to be one in the same, and it works just the same as far as I can tell. Enabling it in the Nvidia Control Panel made the monitor settings show Adaptive Sync: Enabled. One feature I really liked that I wasn't aware of when buying this monitor, is that the settings button is a small joystick. If clicked in it opens the settings window, if towards you or away from you, it allows you to adjust the brightness, and left or right is headphone volume. Overall very nifty for one button. If you need a VESA mount but aren't sure what to get, this is what I ordered: VIVO Dual LCD Monitor Desk Mount Stand Heavy Duty Fully Adjustable fits 2 /Two Screens up to 27" (STAND-V002). Mine is a dual mount but you can choose between double and single. The mount itself is extremely sturdy. Pasé de un Samsung 4K con panel TN a este modelo de LG y el salto es descomunal. Me dedico a hacer contenidos multimedia y lo primero que noté con el panel IPS es que el texto es muuuuuucho más nítido. La claridad y definición de las caracteres no se compara con el del panel TN. Hablando de la edición de video y motion graphics, el color cambió muchísimo; si has investigado un poco, sabrás que los IPS son recomendados para diseñadores y editores y vaya que cambia.

Si sólo vas a jugar y te importa la rapidez de respuesta en FPSs y no tanto los colores (sólo lo usas para jugar y ver alguna serie o videos de YouTube), uno con Panel TN puede ser una buena idea para ti, además de ser muuuuucho más barato con 144 Htz y 1ms.

Si lo usarás para trabajar en creación de medios audiovisuales, es perfecto, pero creo que está sobrado si SOLO lo usarás para eso. Hay monitores de panel IPS a 60 htz que te quedarán de lujo y a menor precio.

Este monitor está dirigido para los entusiastas del gaming y que, además, quieren colores fidedignos y pretendan sacarle provecho a los 144 htz (o 120 o 100), o sea, que su hardware pueda sacarle jugo a eso (el Nintendo Switch no tiene contenido a ese refresh rate ni es compatible con Adaptive Sync, por ejemplo).

El modelo que adquirí fue el 27GL83A que no cuenta con hub USB, pero lo hice así para ahorrar 3,000 MXN y porque realmente no necesito ese hub. No podré actualizar el firmware por esa razón, pero tampoco es necesario; no es como que tu monitor cambie el refresh rate o funcionalidades óptimas por ello.

Conclusión:

Si juegas FPSs, brincar a los 144hz cambiará tu vida.
Si trabajas en medios audiovisuales y tienes un TN, también cambiará tu vida (aunque podrías conseguir uno con panel VA a buen precio y buenos resultados... no los mejores colores pero mejor que el TN).

My 15 year old LG M237WD 23" Flatron Monitor/HDTV finally died on me leaving me in a strange new world where you can no longer find a new, low-cost Monitor/HDTV with a built-in antenna input and tuner. Today you need a monitor with 2 HDMI inputs and a separate HDTV tuner with antenna input to do the job. The question today is which ones do the best job at the lowest price? After extensive online research, I decided on the AOC 24B2H2 24" LCD Monitor and the Mediasonic HOMEWORX HW250STB Convertor Box/Tuner. In short, I am extremely happy with the choices I've made. Before you make your decisions, I highly recommend you download and read the online user manuals available by searching for them online. In particular, you need the online AOC user manual to properly describe and utilize the the 5 tiny buttons on the bottom edge of the screen used to power on and access monitor settings. The paper guide included with the AOC monitor does NOT describe how how to use these buttons. The HOMEWORX manual omits fully describing how to prepare for, record, and playback TV programs on a USB flash drive. If you are computer savvy, formatting, recording, playback and deletion of TV programs is easy to figure out. If not savvy, you may need to ask HOMEWORX for help.

The AOC monitor is very easy to set up. You just need to insert the neck at the bottom of the screen into the base. The screen can be tilted from 20° up to -5° down. You plug in your 1 or 2 HDMI cables from the HOMEWORX tuner and your computer, the power cord, and your speaker or earphone 3.5mm connector cable, and you're done! The HDMI button under the bottom screen edge allows you to easily switch between the tuner and your computer. Audio is automatically switched between devices with the HDMI button. On Windows 10, a 24B2H2 Intel(R) Display Audio interface is automatically installed by the AOC monitor and becomes the Default Playback Device. I have an audio cable running from my computer to my speakers in addition to the HDMI cable. If needed, I can switch the Default Playback Device back to Realtek High Definition Audio to enable me to record audio using Audacity software, which I use to record stock market Earnings Webcasts. (Note: Audacity requires a wire connection between the Realtek audio output and input to enable recording audio off the Internet.) The AOC display itself is excellent, strong clean colors and high definition. The screen is matted, NOT glossy as incorrectly listed by Amazon.

The HOMEWORX tuner has a handy easy to use large remote control along with manual control bottons on the tuner itself. In addition to the HDMI port, it also has RCA jacks and can act as a HDTV converter box for an old analog TV or as audio output for a stereo amplifier. It has a USB-A port for a USB flash drive or other form of storage drive. When not turned on, the HOMEWORX digital display acts as a clock showing the time of day. Signal reception by the HOMEWORX is excellent. This has the best reception of any HDTV tuner I've used so far, and I receive stations I could not receive before so long as the weather and temperature inversions permit.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I've been using this Viewsonic VX2778-SMHD 27 inch monitor since Jan, 2017, Very nice monitor! But, then I built a dream machine. i7-14700K on an ASRock Z790 Riptide motherboard with lots of SSD's and NVME drives. 48 gigs of very fast RAM and two DVDRW's. I'm pretty good at this and I did my very best not to allow any bottlenecks and not spend money on silly things. It absolutely screams; it gets stuff done fast! I also have an older Intel computer, an AMD computer, and a Raspberry Pi in here. So I have an HDMI KVM switcher and an HDMI audio extractor (audio goes straight to a competent home stereo). So, I don't play any games anymore, but I do want to get stuff done!

There came a point where I wanted to make use of this somewhat better video card that's better than anything I've ever used. (Still not for gaming, tho.) I scoured Amazon. I ended up getting an NVidia GeForce GTX 1660 used, that was DIRT cheap! I chewed my nails wondering if it was going to work, but it did and it does! From the first momen, for about 9 or 10 months! I forget how much memory it's got, but it's up there. So, now, I had this video card mostly going to waste (Except for hardware acceleration; that's really nice!) So, I measured how much room I have. If I looked at monitors with really thin frames around the screen and measured and did the math... I decided on 32 inches. I scoured Amazon again and got to this monitor: (KTC H32T13 32 Inch)

I had a little trouble. First of all, I'm lazy. I was still building that i7 and I set the monitor aside after unpacking it and went through all my other stuff I had to do first. (The other 2 computers mentioned above both needed some help.) (And the computer room needed some rearranging.) There's also that fact that there was absolutely nothing wrong with the old Viewsoni; there was no pressure... Anyway! From March 22nd until just now - two days ago - it just sat there. I don't even know where the quick start guide or whatever it is, went to, and I didn't want to conduct a lengthy search. Someone wrote that the power button is in a bad place. It's not that bad at all. I spent a little while finding it; reach your hand around the monitor's right side, near the bottom and feel for it. It sticks way out. The only time I have to reach for it is when I'm leaving the computer room to watch TV or go out or whatever. I can't reach it sitting down, but I'm getting up anyway at that point. Then I was totally puzzled, trying to figure out how to set the settings on the monitor. It wasn't bad, but I wanted to tweak the brightness, contrast, hue, gamma, etc. It took me quite a while to figure out that that power button, which is also a menu button (if you just touch it instead of holding it for three seconds) IS ALSO A JOYSTICK! Remember that! You can move it left, right, up, and down. Once I figured that out, it has a VERY logical, easy to use menu, unlike the Viewsonic mentioned about. The next problem I had was that a lot of things were ghosted in the menu and couldn't be selected. Scratching my head, I theorized that probably the video card was running the monitor and I turned to the NVidia Control Panel on the computer. There are at least three different places to set all that on that i7 machine, but it ended up being the screen display settings that did it.

I love this monitor now! Plenty bright, fast, 2K, really great picture!! If the power button in the back is even a negative, I don't mind a bit. Everything else about it is outstanding! In about a minute, I had all those settings set. Beautiful bright, colorful screen! Perfect! I also have an older Silicon Dust HDHomeRun dual tuner. I encountered something that's never happened before! Watched "The Rifleman" in black and white. NEVER BEFORE have I had perfect black and white! Always some kind of tinge, usually in the dark places. I mean PERFECT black and white! Then I watched some stuff on Charge! (Streaming) and I adjusted color saturation and hue and got the skin tones right. Absolutely perfect picture, no matter what I do, now!!

This is not a cheap budget monitor; this is an inexpensive performance monitor that works extremely well! I completely recommend it and I think it's a super nice deal for the money!!

I tried various resolutions with the Enspire app, the windows 11 camera app, and in zoom. Nothing to justify the high cost.

Max res is 3264x1836, which is apparently 3k, not 4k (who knew there was a 3k?) On screen, images did not appear crisp, certainly not better than any other webcam I use.

If you use a standing desk and have to adjust the camera tilt when moving from sitting to standing, you have to unscrew the mount on the back of the stand in order to adjust it. Kinda of a pain.

I could not get the remote to work (which you apparently need to install inspire to work) despite spending time with tech support. Being able to zoom and make adjustments while on a meeting I thought would be cool - but it did not work (even while using enspire). I'm sending it back, to continue the quest for a high end web cam.

text:
Bought a BenQ monitor - always of the highest quality, I have another one and always been very impressed. Because this time I was replacing an Apple Cinema Display I no longer had built in iSight so needed a webcam. Even though it's pricey I felt assured that a BenQ camera would be just the ticket. How wrong I was!

I can't fault the build - looks really smart. A neat light added on the camera too. Packaging lovely (as if that matters but worth mentioning as it's packed very professionally). The whole thing from the outside screams of a premium purchase.

But there's 3 main flaws.

1) Auto-focus - Really woeful and the main gripe. Even when well lit the camera is constantly hunting focus and gives a breathing effect every time you move. I could almost, almost put up with the other complaints, but this above all makes it unusable for me.

2) Quality - This was really surprising. You can get a decent image when well lit, but let's be honest unless you are a streamer or podcaster etc most of the time you won't be setting up lighting for Zoom chats or Facetime. The image has a flickering effect which is terrible and on my 4K screen the image looked really poor.

3) I spent the extra money on the Pro version which comes with a bluetooth controller. It LOOKS amazing. Tremendous build quality. It has options for adjusting focus, taking photos, freezeframing, zoom, etc etc. BUT, you can only use these (and the rest of the features) if you download a program called EnSpire. So you are left with the poor image and focus problems on a normal zoom/Facetime call.

Additionally the camera is really for PC's not Mac. It seems Mac compatibility is a bit of an afterthought. They don't advise using the desktop version and instead say to access it through a web browser. And even then there are limitations for Mac users.

Some other problems I found - there's no way to adjust the image to be mirrored like you normally see on most webcams. This will be fine for others, I guess I'm just used to seeing my reflection moving the same way I am, even if things are back to front. I also tested recording audio through its microphone on Quicktime and the resulting video was out of sync to the audio. Didn't do any further tests, but just straight out of the box that didn't work for me.

Positives - the little zoom attachment gadget is quite nifty, not sure when I'd use it for though. The microphone apparently has noise reduction. The light is a good addition. The build and everything about it prior to hooking the thing up looks very professional.

But all the problems I mentioned make this webcam completely unusable. It certainly is a case of 'don't judge a book by its cover" - the cover is The Divine Comedy, the contents are Michael McIntyre's Guide to Comedy.

Disappointing.

title: 3.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This monitor isn't going to break any records, the image quality is what you'd expect from 4K, it looks sharper than anything with less resolution and this monitor has a decent color gamut. It's bright and easy to do work on. I do play games on this monitor but also program and consume entertainment. It's a little heavy too, but I like having the large square base for it to rest on. This is where the positives end.

Minus one star for finnicky firmware - I have experienced on at least one occasion where the HDMI port stopped working and I had to grab a DisplayPort cable to be able to access the firmware settings and reset the settings. If the monitor attempted to use HDMI, it would constantly power-cycle. I would at least have expected a fail-safe to detect invalid settings. This monitor is unforgiving to novice users but at its price-point that seems to be its target market.

Minus another star for being a 2023 monitor using outdated DisplayPort 1.2 (2010) and HDMI 2.0 (2013). There is zero doubt the VP327Q is NOT aiming to be a high-refresh gaming monitor; however, newer ports offer better versatility and bandwidth. They have been out for over a decade since this monitor was manufactured and should have been implemented in its design. I don't believe that the value proposition for this monitor necessitated using extremely outdated built-in video-in ports.

Overall, it's a decent monitor and a good start for those looking to see if 4K is right for them. However, it's not going to impress in its video-in ports, unforgiving firmware and it's definitely nothing close to a proper 4K OLED monitor. Even my old 4K/Pantone Color Calibrated ThinkPad P71 from 2017 had better color accuracy.

The picture quality is good, no noticeable ghosting and the response time is equally unnoticeable and so excellent.
The colors on this monitor are definitely a bit more saturated but what this leads to is neon lights and bright colors to look fuller and to pop out more which I think looks really nice and should be how they should look.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I recently bought a 27" AIO computer. I use a dual monitor setup, but all my extra monitors were 24". I know you can do it, but it just didn't look right to me to have a 27" monitor paired with a 24" monitor, so I was on the lookout for a relatively inexpensive 27" monitor.

Started out with an LG monitor at about the same price point. The problem was that the screen didn't line up with my AIO monitor. About 2 inches difference in the height from the bottom of the screen to the desk. Not a huge deal, but again, it just didn't look right to me, so then I was on the lookout for a 27" monitor with an adjustable height stand.

This worked out perfect. I can adjust the height so the monitor lines up perfectly with my AIO monitor. Looks great. Screen quality is very good. Bright (adjustable) and crisp. Perfect for what I do (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, PDF, e-mail, videos and web surfing).

Moving up from 24" to 27" screens doesn't seem like a big deal, but it really is. Makes a huge difference.

100mhz refresh rate is a nice little bonus, since most of the monitors at this price point have 60 or 75. Not a huge difference, but higher is better.

There are several reviews about receiving units that wouldn't power up (DOA). I thought I had one too, but I didn't. The problem is that turning the monitor on is very unintuitive. There is a rocker switch that says power, so you would think that is how you turn on the monitor. It isn't. You have to turn the power on with the rocker switch, then you have to press another small, nearly hidden button to turn the monitor on. I was literally about to pack up the monitor and return it until I figured this out. I suspect that many of those who thought their monitor was DOA didn't realize it was a 2-step process to turn it on. Very confusing.

Overall, this is a good monitor at a budget price point. I recommend.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I bought this monitor for the specs: 100Hz refresh, 1 ms response time, etc. Also it is important to me that the stand can go up and down and tilt. Many monitors don't have a decent stand with these functions, but this one has a great stand. Some monitors have great displays but with stand that has no flexibility. Their makers figure, oh, well, just put some books under the stand. Anyway, once this monitor is up and running, it looks great. All that is to the good. The problem is in the beginning -- getting this monitor up and running.

It comes with something called a "User Guide", which is a 5"x8" pamphlet with only a half page of useful information, which I have posted here. There is no "getting started" sheet, so the user is on his/her own about how to get this thing going. This monitor has only 3 video inputs: HDMI, VGA, and DP (Display Port -- better than HDMI for 4K resolutions). Your computer may not have a DP output. Most users will use HDMI. A good high speed HDMI cable is included in the package.

My difficulty was in getting this monitor going. For an hour or more I thought it was DOA (dead on arrival). Just before requesting a return, I read somewhere that it had an OSD (on screen display). After searching, I found the controls at the bottom right on the back of the monitor. I pressed one of the buttons and presto, part of the monitor screen came to life from the formerly "dead" screen to display the OSD. There I found that the input to the monitor could be selected. Why it wasn't shipped with the auto-select enabled I don't know. I selected HDMI which is what I was using and most users use. Once I did this the entire screen came to life.

In the upper right corner of the monitor, the display rate is displayed in large yellow numbers that cannot be covered over by a window. Many new users like myself will be puzzled as to what this means. For example, my monitor is showing "60". After some research, I learned that this refers to the refresh rate (60 times per second). My current task is to get this monitor to display at its advertised 100Hz refresh rate.

So bottom line this is a monitor that has great specs but requires a user to be familiar with settings and get this monitor up and running. There is practically no information included about how to do this. I have attached the pertinent page of the "user guide" so that prospective buyers can see what they are getting. The "external control" at the bottom of the user guide refers to the OSD buttons at the bottom right on the backside of the monitor. The functioning of these buttons requires some getting used to. Good luck.

Update: after much time and research, I have learned how to update the refresh rate. The standard refresh rate of monitors is 60Hz, meaning the display refreshes 60 times a second. This monitor and other quality monitors offer a higher refresh rate. The Acer can refresh at 100Hz. But how to change and adjust it? The secret is to go to the display settings in your computer. Right click on a blank area of your screen (outside the open windows)

title: 3.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I ordered the KTC 27M1 27 Inch Gaming Monitor with shields- for those reading reviews on the multi-monitor option page. As it is information I always struggle to confirm I will also note it does in fact have G-Sync Compatibility, 2xDP 1.4 ports, and it is HDR compatible (though the screen will not allow for a true HDR display).

The picture color, brightness, refresh rate, etc all live up to the specifications listed for the device, the construction while relatively cheap feeling does present any issues once set up, and the stand it comes with is relatively sturdy and stable on the desk. The VESA mounting option is also perfectly stable, though the product does NOT come with the M4-0.7 x 10mm screws needed for mounting so keep that in mind if you wish to use VESA mounting. Additionally the speakers the monitor comes with built in are cheap but more than acceptable for casual use.

Despite all this, the product is going to receive a low rating from me due to a few issues. Firstly, when receiving this product, the monitor box was placed within another, amazon branded box that was nearly 3 times it's size with no packing material. Due to this the monitor box inside was able to bounce around and may have contributed to the following issues; YMMV as to whether this will be an issue for you as well.

Issue 1: Upon setting up the first monitor I received, adjusting settings, and testing for a while, I noticed on occasion (roughly 10-30 min between) the monitor would flash to black across the entire screen for a moment. After EXTENSIVE testing to try to diagnose whether this was a settings or compatibility issue or an issue with the monitor and my PC, I concluded that the issue was with Display Port #1, as having it plugged into Display Port #2 did not present the issue with the same settings; meanwhile Display Port #1 using other cables or devices, any refresh rate/HDR/Adaptive-Sync/etc. settings continued to present the same issue. At this point I contacted amazon for a replacement, which I received promptly a few days later.

Issue 2: Upon receiving the replacement (arrived in the EXACT same oversized type of box...) and setting the new monitor up (current), it is exhibiting the EXACT same issue only in Display Port #1. Whether this is a QA issue or an inherent flaw with the way the product is designed is beyond my ability to determine, but regardless this means I'll never be able to have two devices plugged in using Display Port. I have NOT had time to check whether either HDMI port exhibits the same issue, though I would hope it does not. In addition to this issue, the monitor also has a red stuck (sometimes called dead) pixel very close to the center of the screen, so when in dark stuff, the red pixel tends to stand out and be noticeable. In other words- I sent in for a replacement due to an issue and received an item with an additional problem instead. I am also now unable to use amazon for another replacement, only a refund. I bought this monitor during cyber monday and cannot afford another monitor to replace it now due to the sales being over. (though perhaps contacting support directly could change this, I am afraid at this point of receiving an even more damaged/problematic monitor again so I'm essentially cutting my losses).

Issue 3: When attempting to contact KTC using the 'contact the seller' button I am taken to a 404 'page not found' error, and KTC's warranty states that 1-3 dead pixels are considered normal and acceptable so I'd have to pray they would simply believe me about the flicker problem as capturing it on video is nigh impossible due to the infrequency of it. I also have never bought a KTC product before or worked through a warranty process with them, but from reading online, it does not produce hope. This has furthered my choice to simply cut my losses, keep my current replacement, and hope it does not get worse or cause other problems over time.

TL;DR- The monitor overall has excellent picture and performance for it's price point, however there are options available with similar performance claims from other manufacturers for similar cost; and unless you wish to test your luck or are ready to accept one port not working correctly being likely, I would suggest choosing one of those other options instead if possible. I will give the final rating of 3/5 stars purely by merit that aside from the dead pixel as long as I stick to Display Port #2 it is an otherwise fantastic monitor.

text:
I’ve tried 5-7 different monitor stands because I have a very unique application where most of these monitor stands will allow you to clamp them to a surface with the clamp shaped like a “U” and the open part of the you has to be facing the surface that it is being clamped to. The other option that almost all of them offer is to drill a hole through the surface, inserting a bolt through the hole and tightening a nut below the surface.

I’m trying to mount the monitor stand on a Corian window sill above a Corian dining table. I am NOT going to drill a hole through my window sill or my dining table. In order to mount the monitor on the window sill and have it swing out over the dining table, I have to have the “U” shaped clamp facing away from the direction of the surface it is being clamped onto. On top of all this, the under surface I’m using is not level as it is actually two different surfaces. With the current mount I used a pice of wood as a shim to make the two surfaces level. Even using a steel shim for this mount to make the two under surfaces level did not provide enough support of this mount to not want to lean when the monitor on the arm was pushed down - even after setting the gas cylinder to the lightest setting.

As mentioned below, because the clamp is a two part system, it offers some flexibility. Unfortunately in my case not enough. When the clamp was in the smallest of the two adjustments, it was an extra layer of thickness between the bottom part of the clamp and the top part of the clamp causing the clamp to not get as close to the surface as possible. When the clamp was in the larger position, it ran out of threads on the screw post and could not tighten against the surface.

I’m attempting to replace a double monitor (2 arms) mount because it only swivels around 220-230 degrees at the base. THIS MONITOR MOUNT SWIVELS A FULL 360 DEGREES!

Pros: A full 360 degree swivel at the base. Both styles of mounting the mount to a surface. Heavy duty construction. Wire hiding covers / channels. Ease of adjusting the hydraulic arms. Adjustability of the clamp system.

Cons: Ugly silver heavy duty clamp system. (Others I have tried have black which doesn’t stand out as much.) Lack of adjustability in the clamp system. Yes, I listed the same thing as a pro. It has a two part clamp system, which has two adjustments. I needed something in-between the two adjustments. Other systems have a clamp that connects to the base of the mount. This system has a two part clamp that connects to the base of the mount. This ended up causing issues for me.

Results: I grade this a five out of five (5/5) stars just on the ability for it to swivel 360 degrees. I was disappointed it would not work for my application but as I have a very specialized application, it is not the mount’s fault.

Brushed metal everywhere except the front. The included stand is a bit awkward to install, but they include a small screwdriver to assist in reaching the awkward spots. It also includes good documentation and a limited warranty, but upon further reading, it appears the warranty is pretty useless because it doesn't cover shipping damage or damage caused by the user, so that's kinda dumb. For the price, however, I would gladly buy it again. And I will once they refund my defective unit. I was really disappointed that I received a cracked screen on my second one. I hear this is not an isolated case, and many other reviews would indicate theirs also had defects or likewise. I'm getting more serious about my photography and part of that is needing to have a monitor that can run a full-color gamut and properly display colors - the problem is, most of these monitors are hundreds and hundreds of dollars. Yikes!!

It really makes a huge difference in fluidity and makes everything feel snappier and crisper, especially in games like Skyrim or Overwatch 2.

All in all, I love this monitor and would recommend it to anyone. It's a great entry-level cheap monitor that works well and gives high-end features at a low-end price point.

Don't sleep on this monitor!

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I've only had the Sceptre E248W-1920 24-Inch Screen LED monitor for a few days now, but I'll update my review if I run into any kinks/issues in the future. For the time being, here’s the just-outta-the-box review:

0. Optional 3-Year protection plan by Asurion: I thankfully haven’t had to use this service, but if you’re super paranoid about the welfare of your devices like I am, that extra three bucks might save your assets later on. You receive the protection plan digitally, so there’s no paper waste involved here.

1. The manufacturer's packaging: The monitor came in a fairly slender box with an instruction manual, the base for desktop use, an HDMI cable, a VGA cable, and the 3-prong power cord. (This didn’t come with a wall mount, or 3.5 M/M audio cable, or DVI cable, so you’ll have to snag those elsewhere if you need them.) The monitor itself was nicely padded with fitted styrofoam, and finally wrapped in that clingy plastic film stuff that gives nerds like me a small thrill to peel off. (ahh, that new electronics smell!) This kind of packaging was a relief to see, as things tend to get knocked around a lot in the shipping process and can lead to fragile devices being dead on arrival. In this case, everything was intact and not all roughed up.

2. First impressions: This monitor is quite light to carry around, even with my wet noodle-strength arms, so that's a plus. There's some very simple assembly required that includes attaching the base and adding the necessary cable hook-ups, and that’s it. (I haven't tried to mount this on my wall because I don't trust my walls to hold up anything heavier than a poster.) As other people have pointed out, the "neck" part that attaches to the base sticks out a bit from underneath and isn't removable, but that isn't an issue for me personally, as I just have it sitting on my desktop. The monitor comes out of the box tilted forward a bit, but if you place your hand on the base and gently push from the top, you can adjust the tilt to your liking.

The base and frame of the monitor is sleek and glossy, but the actual picture part of the frame is completely matte with minimal to no reflections visible while in use. There are a few decals on the frame part, but they’re the sort of indicative labels that boast a device’s features (Energy Star, HDMI-ready, and Win 8 compatible. My PC uses Win 7, and it works great.) There are external menu buttons underneath bottom right side of the monitor frame that are labeled on the frame that includes a button where you can switch from different cable sources (for example, if you have an HDMI cable hooked up from one device and the VGA hooked up to your PC, you can switch from one to the other with that button.) The monitor's built-in menu system is easy to learn and has a nice "transparency" feature that makes the on screen menu translucent enough that it doesn’t obscure whatever you’re looking at.

3. Performance: Oh man, if you're upgrading from a lemon monitor like I did, your eyeballs are in for a treat. After inspecting the monitor, I found that it arrived with no dead pixels or discoloration (yay!)
I used the "auto" feature for picture/resolution adjustments, and it practically set itself up. I played a few games with this thing and I already see a major difference in picture quality, especially with the lights and shades. Sparkly light particles in games actually sparkle. Shadows look like actual shadows. Colors are accurate and vivid, which is a huge plus for me because I do a lot of digital art and design. The LED indicator light on the bottom right corner is visible but not bright enough that it knocks your eyes out in a dark room, so you can forego masking it with electrical tape.

The only disappointing feature I've experienced so far is with the speakers, which have a tin can quality to them---BUT, this isn't a big issue if you already have a sound system set up, or use headphones.

Sceptre E248W-1920 24" review in short:

Pros:
- Lightweight
- Gorgeous picture quality
- Nice big HD screen, especially for the price
- Quick, easy setup
- Can switch picture from different input sources
- Comes with HDMI and VGA cables

Cons:
- Speakers are dinky
-No 3.5 M/M audio cable or DVI cables

Mixed Feels:
- Might look awkward if you plan on attaching this to your wall because of the neck that hangs down, but if that doesn’t weird you out, I guess you could use it to stick post-it notes on, or something.

text:
Company extended my WFH schedule so I’ll have to spend several weeks more working remotely, and figured it is really time to get an extra monitor for my work laptop extended screen and hopefully for my gaming PC upgrade as well.
I was particularly looking for a 4K/QHD monitor since I do a lot of Excels so I gain more cells with higher resolution. However I was told by my roommate that for 27” screen size, going above 1080p doesn’t make much of a difference. Well guess she’s right, here I am, for the same price range of a regular 27” QHD 60hz monitor, with a Sceptre 1080p 27” 165hz gaming monitor
1. My roommate is definitely right, for 27” a 1080p monitor is way enough for the clarity and sharpness. Her 27” 4K monitor does show more contents but all letters and characters are just too small in return
2. A DisplayPort cable is included instead of a regular HDMI one. Nice now I can connect it with my work laptop via HDMI and my gaming PC via DP, one button switch to work and one more button to games, with no more plugging and unplugging
3. The screen itself is very impressive in the slim bezel chasis, no dead pixels or so, native 165hz, fast response time 1ms, rich menu customization and more. Basically it has everything I need to be a work/play 2-in-1, even in Excel/Outlook where most of the pure white color background is used, the screen displays the true colors needed. The only thing is you get 144hz only with HDMI, so make sure DP is used if you want to maximize the refresh rate
4. Monitor comes with AMD FreeSync Premium certified, seems to be an upgraded standard of AMD FreeSync. Wish it could do HDR as well, will find out
5. Monitor also comes equipped with speakers built-in, pretty amazing. I’ll say for gaming, stick to your over-the-ear headphones and for working where you might to be focus with some environment noise, speaker output might be something you need in certain scenarios so speakers are definitely a plus
Overall this is a very nice gaming monitor, even for me half work and half gaming. Will definitely recommend to my friends and might buy a second one to do dual monitor setup to utilize company’s WFH reimbursement policy. Cheers.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I ordered and installed a CRUA curved 27" LED monitor last week and... the ghosting was giving me headaches while gaming and during my day job as a writer, where text would smear up and down the screen in red double vision.

I ordered this Sceptre monitor when I went to their website and saw they actually have full listings of every monitor, manuals saved server-side, and you can contact them directly. I had never heard of the company before, but figured i'd give it a shot.

When I swapped out that CRUA monitor for this one, within 10 seconds, I decided to return the CRUA. It's been about 30 hours since then and I've yet to have a problem. I didn't have to touch any of the settings, the sharpness is great, the colors are vibrant and the CORRECT HUE (unlike the CRUA which tended to be red and muddy). The monitor is pretty light, has a great build quality on the vesa mount - very sturdy feeling plate in the back for the stand to mount to.

It's got all the connections plus more - if it had a curved panel, it'd be better in every single way [and] it's cheaper. Even the branding (the Sceptre logo on the front) is far more subtle, and the starts screen looks clean.

The monitor has quite a few settings, hits 165hz without issue, has no artifacting, light spots, or haze that I can see, zero dead pixels, and a 1ms-2ms response time (though my testing is not flawless), making it really snappy when scrolling or moving sprites on a 2d game like Hades or Cult of the Lamb as well as more graphically intense games that I tested

Came with a 6 feet (2 meter) Display Port cable, a much much smaller power supply than my last monitor, and was packaged fairly well.

So far, so good. This IPS monitor is MILES ahead of any VA monitor out there, and even the blacks look truer. Between the murky colors, slow response rate, and severe lack of settings, I'll never make the mistake of buying a VA monitor again. This, however, was a great deal and filled every role I needed in a monitor.

Will update further if anything breaks!

title: 3.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Here are my initial impressions after owning it for a week. I'll write a more complete review after I've used it longer.

Complaint:
========
I ordered this monitor manual because it has a separate button for selecting the source. I did not want to have to go through menus to switch between VGA, DVI, and HDMI source. It's a nuisance because I have to do it often. Before ordering this monitor, I downloaded the manual from the Sceptre website to confirm its operation. The manual states "The source button selects between the 3 sources on the monitor (HDMI, DVI and VGA).". There's a separate menu button that also allows selecting source, but the manual doesn't state that all the source button does is go into the menu. It doesn't actually select between sources. I wanted a monitor like my Samsungs that have a separate button that toggles between sources without having to go into a menu.

Pros:
====
I like the fact that it has three input sources (vga, dvi, and hdmi) - this is essential for me. I love the fact that the cable ports and power plug on the rear on side-mounted rather than at the bottom like all my other monitors. Side-mounting makes life easier for people like me who change our configuration often - I have five computers (Windows and Linux) and modify them often. I also like the fact that there are no dead or stuck pixels. Text is reasonably sharp, which is important to me as a writer.

Cons
====
My big complaint is how input sources are changed. If the manual stated that the source button does not actually select the source, I would not have ordered this model. I need to change the source frequently, but it's a hassle on this model, requiring pressing first the Source button, then clicking the up or down button to the right source, and finally clicking the Menu button. On my Samsung monitors, a single button does it.

I'm not certain yet how satisfactory the color is. It's generally accurate but not very rich. I'm not very impressed with the color controls. There's a greyed-out option for automatic color control, which also shows in the manual as greyed-out, so it may be an unimplemented feature, or one that's reserved for more expensive models.

Conclusion:
If you don't need to switch source frequently and if you aren't fussy about adjusting monitor color balance, this is an excellent monitor. However, these are important to me. I won't be buying another Sceptre.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Bought this monitor for 2 reasons...I wanted a gaming monitor that had a higher refresh rate and was hoping the ability for this monitor to block blue light would cure my foggy head-aching eyeballs.

I'm a PC gamer and have been for years. Finally decided to try a monitor that blocked blue light and had the ability to raise the refresh rate. I was hoping this would take care of how gaming started to make my head feel.

Since buying and tweaking the blue light (set to strongest setting) and raising refresh rate to 180hz from the old standby of 60hz, I'm glad to say the fuzzy headed-ness and eye strain are almost, completely gone.

Now that I'm 63 I noticed my gaming sessions were leaving me really fatigued and some what loopy and off balance too.

Then I started reading about excessive blue light exposure and the eye strain and loopiness it can cause some people.

Couple that with a 60hz refresh rate on my current monitor, plus being 63 and I was thinking my fun with Elden Ring was coming to a close.

So I decided to gamble on this sweet, fairly inexpensive monitor and BAM! I'm back to slaying dragons again!

When you place the monitor on the strongest anti blue light, it does mean you'll have to manually adjust the color settings yourself for the games you're gonna play.

While not quite as good as having the blue light still on, it's still good enough for me to enjoy playing again.

Setting up your preferences is done fairly easy from the backside of the monitor with 5 easy to reach buttons located on the right side.

2 things to note... if your video card only has a HDMI connection then you will not be able to get the 180hz refresh rate that I'm able to get. You'll be capped at 144hz.

If however you have a display port connector then you're good to go for the higher rate. It does come with both hdmi and DP cables.

2ndly, the monitor tries to take over as your sound card.

I have surround sound and after plugging in the monitor, I had no sound. The fix is to double click the speaker icon located on the bottom right of the monitor (for windows 10), then click the upward arrow and manually choose your sound card.

This will over ride the monitors built in desire to take over your computers sound card.

Once I did this, we had surround sound again.

The manual doesn't say this is the fix you need. I guess they expect you to plug in your green speaker connector to the bottom of their monitor and be happy.

I've got green, brown and black connectors for my sound card, so this wasn't gonna work for me and I wasn't gonna be happy to play Elden Ring without surround sound either.

Anyways, that's my story and a couple of little hiccups you'll need to know about.

I'm happy to say I'm back to gaming again!

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text: I am coming from an IPS Predator panel. I didn't chose to buy this screen because of picture quality but because I wanted a higher resolution. Coming from 1080P, so this one was within my price range. Also wanted HDR whereas my last panel didn't support it. I've been using this one for a day and a half and I must say it's eye opening what I was missing out on. Also a lot of misconception regarding miniled panels. The picture quality is just as good and even BETTER than the predator it replaced. The 180hz refresh rate is less than the 240hz it replaced but I can't notice any difference, no input lag or ghosting at all. Smooth and clear. The brightness of this screen with HDR enabled is INSANE, you just don't know what you are missing until you have tried true HDR. The colors in SDR isn't as good as my IPS panel but once you turn on HDR the colors are better than my predator monitor and insanely bright. If you find it too bright you can turn it down to whatever level pleases you. The 1152 lighting zones give this miniled a HUGE bonus to darks and bright images. Meaning very deep blacks and bright brights! I have a fairly new OLED TV and I can't see any difference between the two technologies. The color options in HDR is greyed out so you can't adjust it but I can see why this is the case. It doesn't need any adjustment at all... The colors are fantastic in HDR. To keep all the goodness of HDR not just while gaming you can turn it on for windows operating system as well. I turned it on for everything. I really did not understand what a huge difference HDR makes. Ran some identifying software Aida, and says it's putting out over 1500 knits brightness in HDR. Games just look 100% better with HDR it's no contest. I'll never go back to non HDR viewing. 1440P is the sweet spot for gaming and navigating windows. Even when HDR is on you can adjust the brightness to your liking. You will have to make certain adjustments for this panel in terms of contrast but I made all the changes within the first few minutes. Also has game setting for boosting smoothness but it's refresh rate of 180 hz is more than good enough by itself. Well done KTC for getting consumers what they want. No frills monitor and great quality!

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This miniLED monitor is phenomenal, and gives you a lot of functionality and picture quality for a relatively low price. If you use your PC for a mix of work and gaming, this is a great alternative to OLED options that can be at risk of burn in. The HDR looks great, the dual mode resolution switch works very well and saves all of your options, and the usb-c 60w port is very useful for plugging in laptops, and charging phones. Some have said that the local dimming could be better, but I think that is only a problem when looking at the screen from an angle. When facing the screen forward, the local dimming does a great job of keeping the dark colors dark.

I've seen some complaints of dead pixels, and bad packaging, but mine was packaged very well, and as of now, there are no dead pixels or black spots that I can see. Everything looks and runs well right out of the box, and I don't have any complaints.

Are there better options out there? Of course! But for the price, its really hard to beat what this display has to offer, especially if you are upgrading from a 1080p setup. This manages to do so much, and I think the pros heavily outweigh the cons.

I bought this monitor about two weeks ago for $165, which is a great price for a 210Hz 1440p display. Out of the box, the performance is very solid — the high refresh rate makes gaming feel smooth and responsive, and the image quality overall is quite sharp for the price point.

Unfortunately, after just three days of use, I noticed a dead pixel. It seems like only the green subpixel is affected, so it’s only visible against darker backgrounds. On top of that, there’s a small patch of around four pixels that appear dimmer than the rest of the screen, which is only noticeable on bright backgrounds.

These issues don’t completely ruin the experience, but they are disappointing given how new the monitor is. For general use and gaming, the flaws aren’t too distracting, but if you’re very particular about display quality, this might be a dealbreaker.

Pros:

Great price for 210Hz 1440p

Smooth and responsive gaming performance

Sharp image quality

Cons:

Dead pixel appeared within days

Small dim area on screen

Quality control could be better

Overall:
For $165, the monitor delivers great specs and performance, but quality control is a concern. If you’re on a budget and can tolerate minor defects, it’s still a solid deal. If not, you may want to invest in a higher-quality option.

text:
I had been looking for a third monitor to add to my set up, and Amazon had recommended this monitor. At first I was a bit reluctant (I wasn't looking to get a curved monitor at all, wanted to focus on size and resolution instead of curvature) but I decided to throw the dice and check it out. It arrived quickly, set up was easy, and after tweaking the display settings, my expectations were heavily exceeded with the performance and quality of this piece of hardware.

Colors are super vibrant, it's snappy and responsive, and the curve of it is a lot easier on my eyes than I had expected. Not only is it fantastic to play games on, but watching movies on it is truly a treat.

My only critique is how you access the display settings. My other monitors have buttons along the bottom edge of their frames with buttons to edit with, but this monitor comes with a single button (more like a thumbstick on a controller) placed inconveniently behind the display. Not only that, but if you hit if you hit the trigger too far left or right it instead turns up and down the volume from it. Just be ready to be up close and personal with it to fix the display settings.

I did have one more issue with it, but it was more of a problem with Amazon itself and not the monitor. I only mention this to bring awareness to potential buyers. On the day I purchased the monitor, it was listed as $240. But literally the day after I purchased it, I went to reread its specs and found that now it was listed at only $200. And even when checking the official Koorui website, the monitor is listed as $200 as well, although it is sold out on the website and only accessible on Amazon. Be cautious to check the pricing so you don't end up having to pay more than it is truly valued at. It might not seem like a super big deal to you, but as a college student struggling at times to make ends meet, it is a big deal to me.

Overall I am heavily satisfied with this monitor and if I ever want to upgrade or replace my other monitors, I will highly look into purchasing another product from this company!

title: 3.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I've been collecting portable monitors all my life as they've empowered my life when it comes to entertainment as well as professional work. I actually found the Kado brand by getting their excellent accessories for my various screens - so I was excited to get this to see what they bring to the table for their actual monitors. What we have here is a solid screen with very bog-standard specs. 1080p, 60hz, 15.6", swing down kickstand and USB-C x2 + mini HDMI. There's nothing specwise that really gives it an edge over other choices - except perhaps that it advertises 100% SRGB - but a good many of the screens have that anyway. Part of the reason I own so many portable monitors is because of some extra feature it offered - whether it be higher refresh rate, 4k resolution, larger size, OLED, or nonstandard inputs like VGA. What this does have that isn't well advertised is that it comes with a very nice carrying sleeve, and a Sceptre-branded plush (chameleon?) keychain shown nowhere in the marketing! What is MISSING is a USB power adapter - which is a huge disappointment considering practically every screen comes with one - and because of another annoyance that I feel this screen should not have had. The problem is that if you try to adjust the brightness or contrast higher when you don't have power from a wall adapter applied, it will throw up an incredibly annoying nag up on your screen which requires extra presses to make it go away and it doesn't just do it once. It will throw up the nag for EVERY SINGLE MODE you try to adjust that it doesn't like per session! I have dozens of portable monitors similar to this and this is the only one that exhibits this poorly designed behavior. Out in the field when you don't wan't to bother with wall power for the monitor is exactly when you don't want to be inconvenienced, and in most cases I do have wall power for my laptop which makes having a warning for it to "drastically consume your device's power" just a wildly inaccurate assumption. The fact that it doesn't come with the accessory it needs to prevent this from appearing is insulting, and while I thought maybe it was an underhanded marketing tactic to sell USB bricks, Kado/Sceptre doesn't even offer one so I really can't explain this decision.

The general performance of the monitor is good for what it is; the screen is bright and colorful and the viewing angles are decent, though they could be better. There are only 2 VESA holes on the back for mounting but its better than having none which is the case with some of the similar models. One thing I like about the menus is that the UI tries to label the functions of the buttons corresponding to where the buttons are on the device - so when you call up the menu, these labels will intelligently change based on the context of the menu which is a welcome feature even if it takes extra presses to get around in some cases. I will say this is one of the thinnest portable monitors I have, which is appreciated. As I tried to push the limits to see what this could do to push beyond its boring default specs, I did find it could be overclocked to 75hz - 77hz without negative effects by using Nvidia Control Panel. The increased refresh rate is even confirmed by the screen itself and seemed to check out when testing it on blurbusters; I've attached pictures of this to the review along with that horrible nag message.

At around the $70 asking price it is reasonable, especially since it does come with the nice carrying sleeve and plushie keychain - but it is very inconvenient that a wall adapter is not included which compounds the nag screen problem. I feel there are better screens out there for the money, especially if you're willing to pay $20-$30 more you can get 120hz+ or even OLED - but if you just want something really middle of the road, this will work nicely if you don't have any higher expectations and can put up with the nag screen.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This display looks pretty good — about as good as a 1080p IPS panel is going to look. I plugged it into my iPad via USB C and played Call of Duty Mobile to test the responsiveness, and it performed perfectly fine for that game. The display settings showed 1080p and 60Hz when connected to the iPad. There’s no noticeable ghosting or artifacts when gaming or scrolling through web content.

The display has two USB C ports and either one can be used for video and/or powering the display. It supports being powered by the device that’s delivering video, but they recommend powering it separately via an additional USB C cable. I’ll touch on that more further down. The display also supports Mini HDMI (and includes a Mini HDMI to HDMI cable), but I’ve read that Mini HDMI jacks tend to wear out quickly, so I would have preferred full-size HDMI. That’s fairly uncommon on portable displays, though, so it’s not a major drawback of this one compared to others.

The included cables are decent quality. I’m kind of picky about active cables like USB C and and try to stick to using cables I’ve bought from reputable brands, but these just make the cut in terms of my willingness to use a cable that’s included with a product.

The body of the display has an odd leather-like texture (despite being hard plastic). I could do without that. If they think it adds prestige, it doesn’t. It just adds crevices for grime to collect in. Balancing that concern out, the display surface resists finger smudges surprisingly well.

My most significant complaint about this product is that the brightness and volume are limited to 30% unless it receives at least 15w of power via USB C. The documentation states that 15w can be at 5V, 9V, 12V, 15V, or 20V, so the majority of Power Delivery power supplies should be able to provide enough power. Some power banks may not be able to, though. Thirty percent is pretty dim, but still useable. When trying to increase the brightness beyond 30%, a warning is displayed saying that going over that may quickly drain the battery of the host device, suggesting that you could go higher, but it doesn’t actually let you increase it further. That was a bit confusing at first.

The speakers are on the back side pointing up — about the worst configuration possible. They put out very little sound even at 100% volume, so they’re more of a backup in case you forget headphones. The speaker of whatever device you’re driving the display with is probably better, though.

In all, it’s a good, functional, convenient (other than the power requirements) portable display that’s worth the price. I haven’t shopped around for these, so I couldn’t say whether there are better options out there, but this one’s not bad. I think you’d be satisfied with it.
