text:
I have given the product 5 stars because it does work as advertised. However, it didn’t perform for me. But it was not the fault of the product. It was all due to my human frailties.

Unfortunately I wear prescription glasses for distance. I primarily wear them while driving. The installation of the monitor either on the windshield or dashboard position the monitor too close for me to properly view with my glasses on. Meaning, the screen is 90% blurry. I can see the road within the immediate of my headlights, but any vehicle or sign forward are just blurry specs I can’t discern. I should not drive without my distance glasses on. And even I did, which I can, I would need my computer or reading glasses to view the screen.

I can see the screen clearly and all it is capturing when wearing computer or reading glasses. But I cannot drive with those glasses on. Although everyone has different sight traits, I believe it is safe to say anyone sharing my prescription glasses scenario will have difficulty viewing the screen using prescription distance glasses.

I believe this product is best suited for someone who can see both close and at a distance clearly. Guess I have to wait until the company creates a screen the size of a Tesla console.

I ended up returning the product. Oh to have my 20/15 vision once again. Sigh.

Update: After posting the review, I did receive an email, with an apology explaining is an unintended mistake and they have fixed the problem. The answer to my original questions are below.

Q1: the front camera picture is stretched. It appears to be magnified and stretched. Is this normal?
A1: Yes it's normal. LANMODO NVS is designed for safe driving at night, so the front camera picture will be a little bit magnified and stretched, and looks nearer than in reality, to remind driver to keep distance.

Q2: the window ball joint is lose and does not hold the camera steady. I have tighten as much as possible. What should I do?
A2: Have you tightened the both screws? One is on the ball and the other one is on the side of suction cup. And you must lock the suction cup to keep it stable when attached to the windshield

text:
I am so impressed, its getting a day one five star review from me. It works great immediately just plug and play. The video and microphone quality is pretty standard. The light is actually very good at making video calls when you're badly lit much improved. It's a decent size (not too big that it's awkward on your desk or monitor not too tiny for the light to be totally useless) and sits very well on a monitor or on the included tripod. It has a ball joint so its also easy to fine tune the angle. I love that it has the slide cover, which is a necessity on a webcam in my opinion.

The lights have three brightness levels for each of the settings (cool white and warm white), pictures in my review are at the most dim for each (so it gets bright enough to light your face). The camera has a green light when it's in use, which is a great comfort for accidentally forgetting you're in a call still or general spyware protection. The cable is USB A with an A to C adapter included. It has a notch to tie it on (so you dont lose it easily) but there isnt a tie actually included. The only potential negative I can see is that the cable length isn't that long and some people might need more length (for my setup with tower on the floor, plugged into the back and cam on my monitor it is the perfect length and has enough slack to put on the desk on the far side of my desk, too).

All around a total win and in my opinion well worth the price I paid.

CONS:

Cheap Wire:
Basically it seems like they are a pair of little kids headphones ... very thin wire that I wouldn't have confidence in, lasting long

I have to preference this by saying that in this price range, all the brands I have tried are the same and its not a problem limiting to this pair of Sonys. It seems like one accidental tug, and even with light pressure, the wire will come apart from the A) Plug and B) Headphones themselve. I really thought it would be a tad more high quality than that. My 828's that I still have are from when I bought them a few years ago, though maybe they changed too, but the wires seem a bit more high quality. The other headphones from Sony (the Sony MDRZX100 's ) have the right idea. I good "thick" cable at both ends, and the funny thing is, those were $3 cheaper.

Sound Quality:
I had to really adjust my review after a few days of using these earbuds. I have to say some songs (counting all the variables like quality of the audio I am listening to and the tons of Equalizer settings on the player itself) SOUND BETTER than other headphones I haved tried. The problem is the "misses" (the songs they do not sound good with) ... the bass has a good "thump" to it, though it (for me) ruins the mids and Treble. The bass is so strong in those songs, I find myself adjusting the treble and mids on the equalizer so much, the overall song (no matter what I do) just doesn't sound right at all. I shouldn't feel that I have to adjust the equalizer for each song on a good pair of headphones.

The 828's I keep bringing up are not the best when it comes to the bass on the songs that these EX37B's sound "great' with ... though overall they sound really good (with my default equalizer settings that I apply) on both of my ipod style mp3 players, my Sony CD/Mp3 CD player, and my computer. I may just for fun bump up the bass on a song or two, but the sound on the 828's sound great the way they are. (though neither of them would probably satisfy an audiophile who needs/wants PERFECT audio)

---------
Answering my own question that I asked before buying: "Are these better than the Sony MDRE828LP, that have been my long time favorites?"

Well no they are not and even if the wire was better, I would say NO they are not.

HAVING SAID THAT, they are not worst ... they just aren't for me

Depending on what your willing to pay (these were about $6 cheaper then the 828's when I bought them), that may effect which model you buy, and to be honest, I know the 828's are discontinued so if I see them at "only 5 left", I may get them even for a higher price, since I am not sure how many "new" 828's are still out there to buy, and I love them.

SUMMARY:
If your like me and a huge fan of the Sony MDRE828LP's and are concerned about getting a different model, I would just say the 828's may be worth paying a little more for.

Until I see other brands in the same price range, have much better quality wires, I will not say "these are junk" ... they just aren't the ones for me and having said that in a few days when I get out shopping, I am sending these back (thanks to Amazon's return policy). I rather just put the money I paid for these toward the 828's (+ pay a little more on top of that) or even get (I may do both here) another pair of http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B004WODP20/ref=oh_details_o00_s00_i02?ie=UTF8&psc=1 's ... ironic i through those in with the order to get free shipping and Those (I am really not an "ear-muff" headphone style fan here) REALLY impressed me. AND These fell short of what I expected.

If these are in the $16+ price range, I would say I do not recommend them (though I'd trust these over other brands, based on my great luck with Sony)... if they really come down in price ... I (probably... price depending) wouldn't buy them again, though I may change from "no i dont recommend these .. to "eh ... for that price, maybe they are worth a shot to some people"

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I don't give 5 stars lightly, but this is about as good a deal as I've seen on headphones in a long time. I got these for a little under $16 (as Prime) and they were well worth that price. I do a lot of live sound work and I tried these because our videographer asked me for something low-end to monitor the audio feed I was sending him. He asked for "closed cans" because he wanted to isolate the feed from the ambient sound in the room. The Amazon description doesn't confirm that, so I went to the Sony site, which had them listed as "Closed supra-aural", so I took a shot. About the only negative thing I can say about these is that they are not true closed cup headphones, but with their noise canceling feature, they still served our purpose.
The Amazon description is accurate, though lacking some information I would have liked to know up front. The answers to my questions were all pleasant surprises. The nicest surprise is that the 1/8" plug at the end of the cable is a 90-degree molded plug, with the typical crimp protection for molded plugs. If you work with as much live sound as I do, you know that 99% of all cable failures occur at the plug. The wires inside these cables are tiny, and repairing them is a major pain, so a failure usually means ditching the cable (or in this case, the headphones). A 90-degree plug goes a long way towards reducing the chance of failure because it keeps the cord in a low vertical profile to the jack it plugs into, and also reduces the amount of bend when the cable hangs down. The molded cover for the plug is slightly tapered where it meets the actual metal stem, which allowed it to fit securely into my iPhone jack without hitting the case. This is where I've seen many 1/8" plugs fail. Another pleasant surprise was that the cable, which is just under 4 ft long, has a nice, thick jacket, which can also be helpful in prolonging the life of the internal wires.
The actual headphones were quite comfortable and light. These are "on the ear" phones because the cups are not large enough to be "over the ear", so if you need that level of isolation, these are not the ones for you. A few reviewers have mentioned the red band to help you quickly identify the right ear, but the headband also has a small "pimple" molded on the left side to help you identify the orientation by touch once you're wearing them. Not a big thing, but a nice touch.
Audio quality was fine; especially for under $20. I often find the cheaper phones either over-accentuate bass (unnaturally), or are very bright. These seem to have a very accurate reproduction of the input. I was working with our videographer to chase down an annoying hum in the audio from the camera, and when we finally got it eliminated, he turned to me and said "These sound great. They'll do fine." Because I'm a bit obsessive about audio, I asked to hear, and they did sound just like the audio feed I was sending him. Since they aren't true isolation cups, I had to attribute the clean sound to the quality of the noise cancellation feature, since there was over 80db of ambient sound at the time. Keep in mind, these are less than $20.
Some final tidbits for those who care about these things. The plug is a true 1/8" plug and it does NOT come with an adapter for 1/4" jacks. It also appears that the noise cancellation logic struggles when the input signal is low. This may be the "distant" or "muddy" sound cited by some other reviewers. I experienced the same thing with my initial tests before realizing the unit I had plugged into was actually sending a lower signal than normal. When I switched to other devices (including my iPhone) which put out stronger signals, the sound was crisp and clean. Some may also find the 4 ft cord a bit short, which would be true if you need to move around a stationary object while wearing them. For my specific need (in this case) or something like a mobile phone in your pocket, this is ideal because you don't have a lot excess wire swinging around. The unit also apparently has a lithium ion battery, but I did not see an obvious way to change it out. I'm sure this is to power the noise cancellation circuitry, so if it goes out, the cost of the battery will probably be about half the cost of replacing the headphones - and you'll probably have to tear them open to change it. Remember, $15. And finally, a curious statement printed on the back of the package: "If you use the headphones with WALKMAN that has a noise canceling function, the noise canceling function will not work." Curious, since Walkman is a Sony trademark.
In conclusion, a great deal (in my opinion), with some nice touches. I've generally been happy with the Sony products I've used, but often found them a bit pricier than similar options. These headphones were a great value for the price.

text:
I bought this to add storage to the top of my monitors. I chose this because of the width of the shelves, the slots that allow for air flow, and the fact that it was advertised as steel. I was disappointed, however, to see the braces are plastic and worry that, over time, the metal screws could grind down the plastic. Assuming these are left in place, and not frequently fiddled with and/or over-tightened, it *should* be fine.

Installation was simple, if a bit fiddly, because the support braces seem to have two settings - super loose, or somewhat tight. I also wish there were markings or measurements so you could easily tell if the two braces/legs were both set to the same angle. I don't know how feasible it is from an engineering standpoint, but a design that allowed one to "click" the support braces into various angles, secured afterwards by a tightening or fastening mechanism, would have been ideal.

In the end, this does exactly what I needed it to do. I don't know if I'd personally trust it with an "up to 15 pound" sound bar, but it definitely is more than sufficient for my needs.

I should add that if you have monitors with slim bezels, you are probably going to experience some screen overlap. I did with my newer Dell 27", but it's not an egregious amount. I also am using this with an older 32" Samsung that is a behemoth by comparison, and the lip only went half-way down.

SONY アダプターケーブル VMC-AVM1（本品） + Libec LANC* / AV 変換アダプター A-3AV + Libec リーベック ズームリモコン ZFC-L をまとめて購入しました。３品共開封してカメラ SONY DSC-RX10M4 に接続して使用できない事に気付きました。
原因を調べると SONY アダプターケーブル VMC-AVM1（本品）の不適合でした。
メーカーサイトの商品ページを見ると、
「マルチ端子搭載ハンディカム（＊1）で、A/V リモート端子アクセサリー（＊2） が使用できるアダプターケーブル

＊2　対応アクセサリー：GP-AVT1、RM-AV2、VCT-50AV、VCT-60AV、VCT-80AV」
と有ります。新しいカメラでは使用できない様です。
アマゾンの商品ページ（本ページ）の箇条書きには何故か＊2のみ記載されており＊1は記載されていません。
他のレビューをお読みになると分かると思いますが、間違って購入した方が大勢居ます。
SONY DSC-RX10M4 で使用可能になるケーブルを探しましたが存在しない様です。
現状では、SONY の新しいカメラで既存のパンハンドル取り付け用リモコンは SONY 製品も含め使用できない様です。
購入検討中の方は同じ轍を踏まぬ様ご注意下さい。

text:
I've been using a Logitech Streamcam since its release and have mostly liked it. It works great in good conditions, but shifted to a more enclosed area with very little natural lighting. And ever since doing that, I've had trouble with it washing out the picture if there's artificial light, or being too dark if there's not. I have a mostly Elgato lighting set up (2 key lights and a light strip) as well as a stream deck. The Logitech has never had good software, but that wasn't a big deal until recently.

Given the streamcam was good enough. I am teach undergraduate and graduate students almost entirely online, so I wasn't needing a professional setup, just for meetings, zoom, and recording videos (using xsplit with a small video of me in the corner of a presentation). Recently, the lighting frustration bothered me more and more and I saw this Mk.2 release. I decided to try it out and see if it was an improvement.

Yes, yes it was very much. While the lighting isn't perfect, the overall quality is so much better I have no regrets at all about shifting to a similar range alternative. The low light works great, the overall image and recording is better, and the software is far and away more user friendly. I can control many functions through my stream deck, making for more dynamic adjustments on the fly in presentations, online live sessions, etc.

Comes with a pretty thick 3.0 USB cable, but if you have a USB C slot in your computer you're wanting to use you'll need to buy your own. Which I did. But having only the 3.0 makes this useable for even older setups.

text:
The Elgato Facecam MK.2 is hands-down one of the best webcams I’ve used, especially for streaming and content creation. The image quality is incredibly sharp right out of the box — no graininess, no blown-out highlights, and the colors look natural without needing hours of tweaking.

Low-light performance is where this webcam really shines. Even in a dim room, the MK.2 keeps the picture clean and detailed without turning everything muddy or noisy. The autofocus is fast and reliable, and the improved sensor makes a noticeable difference from the original Facecam.

Another major plus is the Elgato Camera Hub software. You get full manual control — shutter speed, ISO, white balance, etc. — just like a real camera. Once you dial in your settings, the camera remembers them even across reboots, which is a lifesaver for streamers.

Build quality is solid, the mount is sturdy, and it integrates smoothly with OBS and all major streaming platforms. For the price, it’s an excellent middle ground between generic webcams and expensive mirrorless camera setups.

If you want professional-looking video without dealing with capture cards and giant cameras, the Facecam MK.2 is absolutely worth it. Highly recommended for streamers, content creators, and remote workers who want a clean, reliable image.

This is a great choice if you need a bi-color rechargeable and portable light. I have it mounted on my Gorillapod with no issues. I use it to take product photos for sale on ebay and other marketplaces.

Some Pluses:

+ Feels well built with its single piece aluminum body and solid feeling controls.
+ Nice size and feels like a slim rechargeable battery pack.
+ I appreciated the camera screw threading on the long side and on the short side so that you can mount in either in portrait or landscape mode.
+ The modes are a nice touch which allow you simulate things like bulb flickering, fireplace, tv, candle, and fireworks. Handy if you need a cheap effect for video, but useless for photography
+ It remembers your last setting when you turn on the device
+ Brightness is quickly controlled by the scroll wheel for quick adjustments; much better than having + and - buttons.
+ Plenty bright for my needs
+ The power on switch seems well designed as it is not prone to being turned on or off by accident.

Some Minuses:

- At 1% brightness, I feel that it's too bright for this level. To the eye, 1% feels about 3 times dimmer than 100%, which means it feels closer to 33% than it is to 1%. If you were planning to use this for bed-time reading or as a night light, then this is probably too bright that purpose.
- The modes are neat but the documentation does not mention them or how to activate them. There is a dedicated Mode button, but it's not clear how to scroll through the different modes. Since this is a bi-color light, the fireworks mode is not very convincing, as it does not have RGB to be able to produce different fireworks colors.
- The front diffuser is not removable as far as i can tell. No telling if this clear diffuser will yellow over time which could affect the color temperature.
- Although it has a lovely smooth-feeling surface, i feel it could benefit from having some grip. Some light texturing or grooves would be nice in case you want to hold it in hand to use instead of mounting it.
- I wish that it could be used to charge your phone or other USB device.

Some things other notes:
The manual warns against using the light while charging. I guess it's due to heat which could affect the durability of the battery. However, the light does seem to last long enough for most purposes where you would need to charge it while using it.

text: I picked up this USB C PD to NPF dummy battery cable because I was getting tired of swapping out dead NPF batteries every time I filmed something longer than ten minutes. My camera rig eats through those little bricks like candy, and I wanted a way to power it from my power bank without dealing with bulky adapters. This cable ended up being way more useful than I thought and made my whole setup feel cleaner and easier to manage. The first thing I noticed was the braided wire. It feels sturdy but still flexible enough that it doesnt fight you when you try to route it around your rig. Some cables get stiff and annoying, but this one bends nice without feeling cheap. The length is just right too. Long enough to reach from my power bank to the camera without dangling everywhere, but not so long that it gets tangled in my gear. Plugging it in was super simple. I connected the USB C end to my PD power bank, popped the dummy battery into my camera, and it powered right up. No weird flickering, no random shut offs, nothing. It just worked. I ran it for a whole recording session and the camera stayed powered the entire time. The output range of 9 to 12 volts seems to handle my setup perfectly. One thing I really liked is how stable the power feels. Some dummy batteries get warm or cut out when the voltage dips, but this one stayed cool and steady. I even tried it with a cheaper power bank just to see what would happen, and it still ran fine. The cable didnt heat up or feel sketchy at all. I also used it on my small monitor and it worked great there too. I love that I can power multiple things from one PD bank now instead of carrying a bag full of NPF batteries that all die at different times. Makes my whole workflow way smoother, especially when Im shooting outside or moving around a lot. The dummy battery fits snug in the slot. Not too tight, not loose. It clicks in like a normal NPF and doesnt wiggle around. I shook the camera a bit just to test it and the power stayed solid. No dropouts. The cable strain relief also feels strong, so I dont worry about it tearing if it gets tugged a little. I took it on a small shoot last weekend and it made a huge difference. Instead of swapping batteries every half hour, I just plugged in a big PD bank and filmed for hours. My rig felt lighter too since I wasnt stacking heavy NPFs on the back. It also helped with heat since the dummy battery doesnt warm up like the real ones do. Overall this cable made my filming setup way easier to manage. It is sturdy, reliable, and super convenient if you use NPF powered gear. If you want a simple way to power your camera or monitor from a USB C PD bank, this thing is a great pick.

Questo cavo batteria fittizio USB-C PD a NPF è diventato rapidamente uno degli accessori più utili nel mio kit fotografico, soprattutto quando lavoro con setup che richiedono lunghe sessioni di ripresa o streaming, la compatibilità con i dispositivi che utilizzano batterie NPF-550 è perfetta e funziona esattamente come ci si aspetterebbe da una vera batteria, ma con il vantaggio di un'alimentazione continua che elimina completamente il problema delle batterie scariche durante i momenti cruciali.

Il design del cavo è ben pensato, con i suoi 60 centimetri di lunghezza che offrono la giusta flessibilità per posizionare il power bank o l'alimentatore senza creare ingombri eccessivi nel setup, il filo intrecciato conferisce una sensazione di robustezza e qualità che ispira fiducia, specialmente quando si considera che questo tipo di accessorio viene spesso sottoposto a stress meccanici durante l'uso sul campo, non ho ancora riscontrato problemi di usura o danneggiamento nonostante l'utilizzo frequente in diverse condizioni.
L'input USB-C con supporto Power Delivery è probabilmente la caratteristica che apprezzo di più, dato che permette di sfruttare praticamente qualsiasi power bank moderno o caricatore PD per alimentare i miei dispositivi, la tensione di ingresso da 9 a 12V con uscita da 2A si è dimostrata più che sufficiente per alimentare stabilmente il mio monitor esterno durante le riprese video e anche alcune luci LED che utilizzo per l'illuminazione d'apporto. La conversione della tensione avviene in modo trasparente e non ho mai notato cali di performance nei dispositivi collegati.

Ottima la stabilità dell'alimentazione durante le lunghe sessioni di lavoro, dove prima dovevo costantemente preoccuparmi di cambiare le batterie NPF ogni paio d'ore, ora posso concentrarmi completamente sul lavoro creativo senza interruzioni, collegando semplicemente un power bank capiente che mi garantisce ore e ore di autonomia, questo è particolarmente vantaggioso durante i live streaming o le riprese di eventi dove non posso permettermi interruzioni tecniche.
Le protezioni integrate contro sovratensione, surriscaldamento, sovraccarico e cortocircuito offrono quella tranquillità in più che è fondamentale quando si lavora con attrezzature costose, non ho mai avuto problemi di questo tipo, ma sapere che ci sono queste salvaguardie mi permette di utilizzare il cavo con maggiore serenità, specialmente quando uso power bank di terze parti o alimentatori di varia provenienza.

Un aspetto pratico che vale la pena menzionare è quanto questo accessorio semplifichi la gestione dell'attrezzatura durante gli spostamenti, eliminando la necessità di portare con sé multiple batterie NPF di ricambio e i relativi caricatori, basta un buon power bank USB-C e questo cavo per avere un'autonomia praticamente illimitata.
Il rapporto qualità-prezzo è decisamente convincente, considerando che una singola batteria NPF originale costa spesso quanto questo cavo, ma offre molto meno versatilità e autonomia, per chi lavora regolarmente con dispositivi che utilizzano batterie NPF e cerca una soluzione affidabile per l'alimentazione continua, questo cavo rappresenta davvero un upgrade significativo del proprio workflow.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I've been using the original Scorp C for over a year, so I was excited to test out the C2. After several weeks of use, here's my take.

What's Better:
Higher Payload (3.5kg vs 2.5kg) - This is the biggest improvement. I can now use heavier mirrorless setups and even smaller cinema rigs without worry.

Built-in AI Tracker - Game changer! The original Scorp C required a flimsy magnetic attachment that would fall off. Having it integrated directly into the gimbal is so much more reliable.

Balance Check Function - The app now gives real-time feedback on your gimbal balance. This feature alone has saved me tons of time during setup.

1/4" ARRI Mount - Small addition but huge in practice. Being able to mount monitors or accessories directly makes outdoor shooting much more manageable.

What Stayed Good:
The axes still lock in-line for easy transport, no horizon calibration needed (tested with Sony a6700), and the Scorp app remains excellent for power users. Stabilization performance is solid - tested it walking on unpaved paths in flip-flops and footage was usable with minimal post-stabilization.
Arca-Swiss Compatibility - Still uses standard Arca-Swiss plates, so you're not locked into proprietary systems. Can use aftermarket plates from SmallRig, Ulanzi, etc.

The Disappointing Parts:
Build Quality Feels Cheaper - The materials and finish don't feel as premium as the original Scorp C. It's functional but less polished.

No More Integrated Bipod - They removed this feature from the original, which I actually found really useful.

Poor Joystick Design - Still imprecise and easy to overshoot your target. There's a wheel for fine adjustments, but it only works for vertical OR horizontal movement at a time, not both simultaneously.

Basic LCD Screen - Technically it has one now, but it's very barebones compared to DJI or Zhiyun options.

Pro Tip:
Max out the dead zone setting in the app! Out of the box, it introduces micro-movements that hurt footage smoothness. With dead zone maxed, it's much more stable.

Bottom Line:
If you're coming from the original Scorp C, this isn't an essential upgrade unless you need the extra payload or ARRI mount. For first-time gimbal buyers, it's a solid choice with good app support and standard mounting compatibility, and the improvements over the first generation are meaningful.

Would I recommend it? Yes. It's capable and the app ecosystem is excellent, but the build quality regression is a little disappointing.

Who should buy this:
- Content creators needing higher payload capacity
- Users who want integrated AI tracking
- Anyone wanting good app control and standard mounting systems

Who should skip this:
- Current Scorp C owners happy with their setup
- Users prioritizing premium build quality
- Anyone wanting precise joystick control

text:
La verdad, el gimbal Feiyu SCORP-C2 me ha sorprendido bastante. Siempre que piensas en gimbals, te vienen a la cabeza DJI y Zhiyun, y no es para menos, son los que popularizaron estos cacharros a precios razonables. Yo ahora mismo tengo un DJI RS4, he tenido un RSC 2 y algún Zhiyun Crane 2, todos buenos gimbals, cada uno con sus puntos fuertes. Pero este Feiyu me ha dejado flipado, no esperaba que fuera tan bueno y que no me hiciese echar de menos a los otros.

Para empezar, el diseño es curioso pero realmente útil. Trae integrado un mango que acabas comprando para todos los DJI porque, si no, terminas con la espalda destrozada. En el mango tienes la pantalla y los botones principales, todo a mano. Además, al ser tan abierto por arriba, tienes un espacio enorme para montar incluso un 70-200mm y estabilizarlo, que es una locura. Es súper cómodo de usar, se siente ligero aunque pesa un pelín más que el RS4; el reparto de pesos hace que no lo notes tanto. La estabilización es de otro nivel, con bloqueos independientes para equilibrar los ejes de forma individual, lo que agiliza un montón la tarea. También tiene autorregulación de los motores, que hay que hacer cada vez que cambias los pesos para que el gimbal sepa qué tiene que compensar. Los motores son muy potentes, nunca se me han calentado ni se han venido abajo, y aunque anuncia una carga de 3,5 kg, he metido hasta 4 kg bien equilibrados. Es un gimbal válido para cámaras sin espejo normales o grandes como una Nikon Z9, Canon R1 o R3, o incluso una Red o una Canon C400, Sony FX6... ¡prácticamente carga de todo!

La autonomía es de locos, mucho más que DJI. Aunque DJI anuncia 12 horas y Feiyu 14, la diferencia es monstruosa, te da para jornadas eternas sin preocuparte. La aplicación móvil es sencilla, y la conexión por Bluetooth a la cámara también, aunque, como siempre, solo sirve para darle a grabar y poco más. Si conectas la cámara por cable, desbloqueas muchos más ajustes, pero ojo, casi todo funciona solo con Sony, y algunas cosas con Canon, Nikon o Panasonic. Además, trae una cámara para seguimiento de sujetos por IA, que funciona bastante bien para autograbarte o seguir a alguien. No soy muy fan de esos seguimientos, pero la verdad es que ayudan un montón.

El único pero que le pongo es la pantalla, que es enana. Aunque es perfectamente legible, resta algunas cosas que podrías hacer desde el gimbal y te obliga a ir al teléfono. Creo que es algo hecho a posta para que compres el FeiyuTech Scorp 3, que cuesta el doble. También tiene un modo de grabación vertical, tanto nativo por la montura como con un botón que cambia la orientación de la cámara, lo cual está guay para redes sociales.

En resumen, este gimbal iguala al DJI RS4 o al FeiyuTech Scorp 3, que valen el doble, carga más que el DJI, viene mejor equipado para no necesitar accesorios, y el software de estabilización va genial. Por lo que cuesta, lo recomiendo mucho. Si buscas un gimbal que cargue de verdad y no quieres irte a modelos viejos de DJI o Zhiyung para ahorrar, aguante lo que le eches y no te rompa el bolsillo, el Feiyu SCORP-C2 es el camino a Seguir me ha sorprendido muchísimo y por solo tener la pantalla pequeñita no se le puede descartar en absoluto.

Using a new NP-F970 clone (8800 mAh) I was able to run my rig in constant record/transmit mode for about 1.5 hours. I am sure I can stretch another 1/2 hour to 45 min with some of the newer 10k mAh batteries on the market. This configuration will burn through older/less efficient batteries in less than an hour. Some of my older batteries (> 6 years) didnt last 1/2 hour. Since I never record in full 1 hour spurts, this should probably last 2-3 hours in standard record/pause mode w/good batteries, and longer if I do not wirelessly transmit.

These connectors are excellent for those consolidating to an NP-F battery strategy. I have purchased three in total, as I also use one on my gimbal.

Advice - understand the wattage draw from each of your devices. These plates usually cannot handle more than 20w consistently with a peak of about 28w. Stringing together too much stuff may cause problems.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I am looking for a way to power my Atomos Ninja V from a power bank (more on this later).

This kit comes as 3 pcs:
a) US 2 prong power cable,
b) 2 prong input 100-240 volt AC to 8 volt 3 Amp DC with 5.2 2.1 female dc plug and
c) 5.2 2.1 female dc plug to NP-F550 dummy adapter.

The build quality is ok. Average to after market China product, and the adapter comes with blue LED that lit when there a power.

The power output is rated @ 8 volt 3A, sufficient for Ninja V that require 24 watt. Ninja V is save with input power of 6.2V to 16.8V dc.

When connected the whole kit to power Ninja V, it works flawlessly, and Ninja V reported the power as 7.2 V. Power consumption is 17 to 21 watts which is still lower than rated output of this kit (24 watt).
During the test, the adapter is not becoming warm which is a good sign.

Then, i tried the dummy battery part, and connect it to my power bank that has 12 volt output with 5.2 2.1 dc plug. I use it again to power Ninja V (which is accepting up to 16.8 volt). It is working as expected, and Ninja V report the power as 12.2 volt. So conclusion is, the dummy battery is only passing thru whatever voltage it is fed into. So be careful if you want to use it this way. You have to match the voltage of your device with the voltage of the source power you feed into the dummy battery (risky business if you are not familiar with basic electronic).

So I use this setup to power the Atomos Ninja V when recording long time static (tripod mounted), with my Sony A74 (also using dummy battery). So far so good. Don't know how long it last, time will tell. At least I can have more recording time compare with NP-F970. NP-F970 alternative when no AC power is available.

Full disclosure - I received this product as a member of the Amazon VINES review program. The comments and opinions are based on my knowledge of similar products and experience using the product listed.

Recently I purchased a Field Monitor for use with my Canon DSLR camera and while it uses a rechargeable battery, I can see a time when I might want to or need to use an AC power source to run the monitor. I am a retired engineer and old habits die hard. I know that if a device has a battery source and that is the only source you have available to power the device, that Murphy states that the battery will die exactly when you need it most with the greatest negative impact to whatever you are trying to accomplish.

So, with that in mind, I saw this AC 'dummy battery' and since I was intending on getting one anyway, I took advantage of my good fortune and got one. It has a 'dummy battery' that replaces the real battery in the battery socket on the back of the field monitor and works just like a fully charged battery would. No switches or configuration changes required. Hook it up and you're good to go. And with a 12-foot cord you won't be tied to the wall with a short cord. It features the customary protections found in most power supply devices such as overvoltage, overcharge, overcurrent, temperature and lightning protection. It has several agency listings displayed on the case but notably it is missing the big one, Underwriters Laboratory (UL). I always look for that and if possible, I choose devices with that agency over any others.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I bought the Klipsch Reference Cinema speaker set a few weeks ago and needed some stands, so this is my experience with that. First off, the feet on the bottom are plastic not rubber, so expect that. Next off there is no padding the speakers sit on. Just metal. My speakers have a rubber pad on the bottom so this didn't affect me, but keep in mind you may need to buy some rubber strips. Next the hole on the back of my speakers is 1/4-20, and the stands only provided short 1/4-20 bolts for Sony speakers. I wanted to use the spacer since my cable come out the back and didn't want them being pinch between the speaker and the stand, so I went out and got some 1/4-20 x 1 1/4 bolt from the hardware store which worked great. Next I felt with the speaker on there the stand was a little top heavy. It definitely wouldn't tip over on its own, but I could definitely see someone bumping it hard enough during a house party to knock is over by accident. To solve this I bought some 2" center, 10lb weight plates. These fit perfect over the tube coming out of the base and make it much more stable, and should make those plastic feet less of a deal.

After all this,, they hold the speakers very tightly,, and are plenty stiff/balanced for my to feel comfortable and not worry about my speakers falling off/over. Overall a good sturdy speaker stand with an inoffensive look. I gave them 5 stars just because I really couldn't find anything better on Amazon, but just understand you may want to make a few modifications to help them reach their full potential.
timestamp_raw: Reviewed in the United States on August 6, 2023

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text: Got these for my Klipsch Reference Cinema surrounds. First thing, the feet are NOT rubber! They are plastic. Not a huge deal. I put sticky felt pads on them. Makes a huge difference. The 1/4 inch bolts that come with the stands were too long for the holes on these speakers and the washers are too small for the 1/4 inch bolts. I went to Home Depot and got 1/4 in - 20 X 1 inch bolts and large washers. The holes on these speakers are very low on the back. Instead of using that ridiculous hole on the bracket, I raised the bracket all the way up, used the large washer and spacer to screw the bolt through the bracket, into the speaker. This way the bracket doesn't look awful, hanging down in the back. I also put self stick vinyl foam weatherseal tape on the bracket brace to secure it and reduce vibrations. Everything works perfectly. With a few minor modifications, these stands are perfect for these speakers. These stands a very sturdy. That only way they fall over is from an earthquake or someone knocks them over. Pictures taken before wires were secured inside stands.

text:
Okay folks, picture this: it’s 11:30 PM. I’m in my garage, wearing pajama pants, a “Team Coco” hoodie (that I did NOT pay for), and holding a camera like it’s a live ferret. I’ve got a microphone in one hand, a tiny LED light in the other, and a deep yearning to be respected by at least one teenager on TikTok.

Enter this little miracle: the Dual Cold Shoe Extension Bar Mount.

Now, I don’t say this lightly, but this thing is the Tom Hanks of camera brackets. It shows up, does the job, doesn’t make a fuss, and somehow makes everyone look better. It’s made of aluminum—aluminum!—which I assume is what NASA uses for astronaut mustache combs. Light, durable, and cooler than I’ll ever be.

The dual cold shoe design is great if, like me, you need to attach multiple accessories at once, and have the spatial awareness of a concussed moose. One side gets the mic. The other gets the light. Boom. It’s like your camera just got shoulders. Broad, competent shoulders. Shoulders that go, “Yeah, I’ve got this.”

And the cable slot? GENIUS. Why is it genius? Because now I don’t have to wrap my mic cable around my camera like some sort of desperate tech spaghetti monster. It keeps everything tidy—unlike my emotional life.

And it screws right into the 1/4" tripod thread, which, as any non-athletic, non-mechanically inclined late-night host will tell you, is the only thread I understand. If I can mount this bracket in under three minutes, anyone can. Seriously—I once tried to put IKEA furniture together with a pizza cutter.

Final thoughts: If you’re a content creator, a hobbyist, or just someone who wants to mount multiple things to one spot while still looking vaguely like you know what you’re doing—buy this. It’s affordable, solid, and makes you feel like a professional… even if your “studio” is your laundry room and your lighting kit is a table lamp with a sock on it.

Five stars. Would cold shoe again.
(Also: cold shoe is a very cool phrase. I’m naming my next band that.)

The 2 pin LEMO-style end operates smoothly and plugs in securely, so no worrying that it might fall out like some D-tap plugs do. The NP-F battery end clicks in tightly and fits just right. Build quality feels fairly standard, with a somewhat light and moderately cheap feeling NP-F end (the dummy batteries almost always feel light and cheap since they aren't filled with hefty battery cells) while the 2-pin end feels just as solid and high quality as an actual LEMO plug (at this price it has to be an off brand version) and functions just as well.

This feels like a cable made for professional use rather than a cheap add-on. The 4-pin XLR connector is all metal and locks in with a solid click, which is always reassuring if you’re powering proper kit.

I’m using this to power a monitor from a V-mount battery, and the right-angle XLR is the real advantage here. It keeps the connector tucked in close to the body and avoids unnecessary strain on the socket. That matters when you’re working with cinema or broadcast equipment like Blackmagic URSA bodies, or external monitors from SmallHD, where cables are constantly being moved, packed, and re-rigged.

The coiled cable length is well judged. It stretches when you need a bit of reach, but stays compact the rest of the time, so you’re not dealing with excess cable hanging off the rig. On handheld or shoulder setups, that makes things noticeably tidier and less prone to snagging.

In use, it’s been completely reliable. No flickering or dropouts, and nothing to think about once it’s plugged in. Given the compatibility list covers a wide range of established broadcast cameras, monitors, and recorders, that reliability feels entirely in line with its intended use.

Overall, this is the sort of power cable you fit once and then forget about. For anyone running monitors or accessories from V-mount batteries on professional video gear, it feels like a sensible, dependable choice.

text:
Das Kabel ist ungestreckt circa 40 Zentimeter lang. Nach 8 Zentimeter vom D-Tap Stecker, oder 17 Zentimeter vom verriegelbaren Stecker aus, befindet sich der mittlere dehnbare Spiralförmige Teil des Kabels.
Dieser Teil lässt sich mit großem Mut auf 70 Zentimeter ausdehnen. Nach kurzer Zeit hat sich die Spirale dann auch wieder vollständig zusammengezogen.
So haben wir eine nutzbare Länge von 45 bis maximal ca. 100 Zentimeter.
Das Kabel ist hat einen Durchmesser von 4 mm. Es vermittelt haptisch und optisch eher den Eindruck einer Gummi-, statt Kunststoff Ummantelung. Die glatten Stücke des Kabels lassen sich durchaus in einen Radius von 15 mm biegen, ohne dabei auch nur Ansatzweise den Eindruck zum Knicken zu erwecken. Natürlich neigen auch die geraden Kabel-Stücken dazu ihre Form beizubehalten, haben also wie die Spirale einen gewissen Widerstand.

Der D-Tap-Stecker ist ein üblicher Vertreter seiner Art.
Er ist sehr passgenau und sitzt stramm und somit verlustsicher in entsprechenden Buchsen.
Das Steckergehäuse ist verschraubt und hat auf der abgerundeten Steckerseite eine + und – Kennzeichnung.
Die Pins bestehen auf der Steckseite aus einem Mittelstift und einer geschlitzten, mittig aufgebogenen, federnden Hülle. Das gewährleistet guten Kontakt und vor allem festen Halt.

Der verriegelbare, 90° gewinkelte, DC 5,5 2,1 mm Monitor-Strecker wirkt ebenfalls sehr hochwertig. Als drehbare Verriegelung dient ein stabiler, außen gerändelter, Überwurfring.
Dieser Stecker ist für einige Monitore mit entsprechender Buchse vorgesehen. Durch die drehbare Verriegelung entsteht ein sicherer Halt auch im rauen, professionellen Einsatz.
Viele Monitore haben einen identischen Anschluss, jedoch ohne Verriegelung. Da hier an diesem Stecker der Überwurfring nicht entfernt werden kann, müssen dort entsprechende Kabel (Stecker) verwendet werden.

Ich kann das „D-Tap-Stecker auf verriegelbaren DC 5,5 2,1 mm Stecker, Monitor-Stromkabel“, uneingeschränkt empfehlen und gebe gerne verdiente 5 Sterne.

text:
This NP-F plate does what it says, but it feels pretty bare bones for the current asking price. It takes NP-F batteries and provides an 8 V (7.2 to 8.4 V) barrel output and a 5 V USB-A port, so it can power a camera or field monitor without any issues in basic use. The molded plastic housing feels well made and not cheap, and the included hot shoe mount and 1/4" screw give enough flexibility to mount it on a camera, cage, or small rig.

My main disappointment is with the I/O. The product page mentions a USB-C connection, but the plate I received only has an 8 V barrel output and a USB-A port, with no USB-C at all. That really limits how versatile it is, especially now that pretty much everything runs on USB-C PD. There is also no battery level indicator on the plate, so you have to guess how much is left in the pack. These are basic features that all my other NP-F plates have.

By itself, this is an okay NP-F plate for simple 8 V barrel and 5 V USB use. It works. The problem is value. There are other NP-F plates in a similar price range that offer more modern features like USB-C PD input/output and 12 V out in addition to 8 V. Compared to those, this one really needs to be on a very good sale for me to recommend it. The build is fine, but the design and feature set feel like they need an update to catch up with more current options.

I have to deduct 1 star for the poor value proposition and another for the confusing functionality claim that mentions USB-C connection in the written description when the plate itself only has barrel and USB-A outputs.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This is my first case from Musiin. The case itself is good-looking and nicely-made. The main draw for me was the insert/divider that creates a separate compartment for the coiled cables of studio monitors which are often too heavy to stay put in the mesh pocket (if they even fit in the first place), but I did not foresee how little room said divider would leave for the actual headphones.

Overall internal dimensions are included in the listing, but the all-important measurements for the headphone compartment itself are missing. By my measurements, that area is 7.75" x 4.25" -- this means that if your headphones don't fold the same way as the Sony model in the marketing shots, they're not likely to fit... And if you choose to ditch the divider, the case will then be too big and your headphones will slide around inside.

The insert is just a folded piece of EVA that's glued to itself to form the divider, and as a result, it curls clumsily inside the case and creates an aesthetic-only issue that I cannot bring myself to unsee. It could have easily been made to lie flat by gluing it to the bottom of the case, but I'm glad they didn't -- I'll eventually be cutting it to shrink the cable compartment to allow room for bigger headphones.

I still recommend this case, just make sure you have headphones that are compact enough; alternatively, keep your scissors handy.

text:
This cable comes with almost any barrel-type connector you would ever need. The tips connect to one end while the other end is a USB-C connection.

If you want to charge at anything other than 5 VDC, though, both the charger & the device will need to PD charging compatible.

For example, I wanted to charge my UE Hyperboom speaker, thich needs 20 VDC and used a less common barrel plug (large outer diameter, but a needle-thin positive center post). The pin part of my factory charger broke off, but this cable came with the correct tip.

Unfortunately, the speaker is not PD compatible. I had to "trick" it into charging at 20 volts using my USB tester. Otherwise, this cable will only provide 5 VDC to the speaker, which doesn't do anything.

But I am not docking the cable for that. It is clearly outlined in the description.

It is a great cable if you need to charge a PD device with a PD charger, but don't have the original cable.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I took way too much time before buying this. Yes, it's totally worth it.

1. The colours are outstanding. Please don't let people throw you off by remarking on a pinkish hue. For me, I've not noticed it. Colors look vibrant, darks are indeed dark and all that jazz. How this translates for you most likely:

+you want to play games way too long,
+watch movies for way too long,
+sink hours upon hours needlessly web surfing.

Why? Just cuz. The screen looks that freaking amazing! And you can't believe it costs under $300.

Then there's the stand. It's proven more useful than I would have predicted. Sometimes I like to feel super official and read my kindle books on a bigger size screen - especially for DK books or you know, those cool "coffee-table" kind of books I think they are called. Anyway, this monitor is AMAZING for that. I thought adjusting the screen to different orientations would prove more challenging and keep me from wanting to do it often, but not at all. Luckily it doesn't take massive strength or strain or anything to move the monitor around, and sometimes that allows for experimentation using your monitor in ways that you may not even realized you'd appreciate. Again, for me, that's proven true in regards to reading kindle books on this monitor. I think I'd now ALWAYS prioritize having a useful, functional stand. I know that monitor arms are a thing, but for some of us, we just want to buy the monitor and be able to use it for as long as possible without having to buy anything else ;) With this, you have one of the very best monitor stands I could imagine.

I also want to mention the warranty - a 3 YEAR WARRANTY that goes so far as to cover ACCIDENTAL DAMAGE in the first year. Now that is value unparalleled, and provided that they folow through on those promises to the customer, it's really hard for me to recommend anything else. To anyone who is shopping on a budget but wants something that doesn't feel budget WHATSOEVER, I'd say go this route.

When I was monitor shopping, I tried an array of different monitors. Initially I was going for a 42 inch monitor, trying to go for the "best of the best". The Gigabyte Aorus 43vu, for instance, is a great monitor as is the LG C3 in that size category. I tried 34" and 32" inch monitors. Interestingly, even if price wasn't a consideration, I'd still argue that this 27 inch screen provides the better QUALITY and VALUE, which is kind of crazy to be getting both things at once, you know? I kept thinking that a 27 inch screen wouldn't be as "fun" as a bigger screen, but as it turns out, for gaming from a desk, I will now ALWAYS choose 27 inches over 32 inches and anything bigger. Basically, I was wrong thinking bigger translates to a more enjoyable experiencd. ! I know these are specific details, but there may be someone else out there going, hey! I love this monitor, but it's ONLY 27 inches! I can't tell you for sure that it is enough, but for me, the 27 vs 32 inch monitor debate ends with the 27 being the clear choice. Compared to the 43 and 42 inch sized monitors, I definitely prefer gaming on this 27 inch monitor too, I occasionally game on the bigger television I own. I so prefer gaming on the 27.

Look, I don't want to encourage anyone to buy this who is gonna hate it. I'm sorry if this love letter to this monitor leads you astray and your experiences end up different than mine. But for real, if you want to skip skimming all the reddit forums and the few reviews you can find on this monitor, just take this recommendation. I came in to this skeptical and am seriously blown away.

Let me address a couple of things I was worried about:

+it being too big, too thick. It isn't. For me, it's perfect. It doesn't remind me of the 1990 CRTV days, and the depth it does have...it just feels right for the picture it creates, as strange as that is to say that way. I have a desk depth of 30 inches. I'll try to upload photos later in case that will help someone determine if it seems too big.

2. pinkish hue: totally don't see it. Nothing distracts, nothing makes me go oh, this monitor has a bad picture. It's good. For the money, it's great! You could tell me this should cost someone $600, and I'd believe it. It performs far above its asking price.

Think about that. How often do you buy something that feels really like it should cost twice the price even?
Not often enough! Do yourself a favor! Go for it.

(To everyone who wants to make a size matters joke, ditto. Enjoy your day and this review!)

Amazon had no reviews but this lightbar was recommended in a few websites so I took the chance.

Review is from a few days of using this product, and so far I like it a lot. I'll describe my specific use / circumstances and how the product meets / doesn't meet my needs:
- work from home setup with two monitors
- monitor is thicker than most (Samsung LS27E591; 27in flat monitor with curved back)

Previously purchased a Quintis lightbar which is a good product in its own right, but did not fit my monitor. The spring did not extend far enough for the counterweight to work properly (I augmented with some cardboard but still wobbly). The Mi lightbar fit perfectly and is stably clipped on my monitor.

I like the remote control a lot. It's wireless and intuitive to use. Personally I like it more than the switches / touchpoints they have on most lightbars-- especially if your lightbar is instable and pushing / touching risks it falling off the monitor. However I'm seeing the wireless remote also poses an issue in my case because I need two. My situation probably isn't super unique, as I expect a lot of professionals work with two monitors at this point.

All things considered, I think the product is great. If you have a thicker monitor and don't use dual-screens, I think the lightbar brings great value and I can recommend without hesitation. If any of shortfalls I described above apply to you, still a good product but worth considering others.

text:
i've had this watch for 9 months now, and i've had some other decent brands before those failed on me
I bought it for a sleep tracker and fitness monitor with really good reviews on youtube (very likely paid).
i ended up using it as a basic watch with message/calendar notifications and convenient media control, which works for me, but that should be about the expectation

Pros:
- stylish watch, rich in functionality

Cons:
- integration with android is suboptimal, red icon in the notification bar always
- watch voice call is really nice to have, however it messes up other BT devices, i couldn't have both watch and car connected. Car is must have, therefor had to turn this off.
- with watch voice call disconnected, watch does not show calls, it only notifies of a missed call after it gets dropped
- exercise auto detection buzzes every time i walk anywhere, had to turn it off
- i have a doubt that heart beat is accurate, it showed 90 bpm when my heart was pounding
- exercise tracker has some SW bug, when it's turned on it's a matter of time when the watch goes reboot and looses all traction, it works okay for a short exercise, but for a long jog or a bike ride, it'll reboot
- gps experience is frustrating, i ride a bike, i stop for a sip of water and it stops the tracking, reboot with time make it even more frustrating
- sleep tracking is nice but not accurate. it made me smile when it recognized me sitting in a dentist chair as a nap time
- touch screen action is not well filtered, sometimes you find your watch deep in settings, if you go shower with the watch, it'll change things on the phone, SW does not filter accidental touches well

text:
After swapping from iOS to Android a few months back, the only thing that was stopping me from completely escaping the Apple Ecosystem was my Apple Watch. The Xiaomi Smart Band 10 swopped in allowed me to continue on my day with all the fitness tracking features I needed, at a MUCH cheaper price and in my opinion, more fun to use.

The watch faces are whacky, unique and so entertaining. I have now settled on a photo slideshow watch face which fits me perfectly. the apps are somewhat lacking and you can't have slimmed down smartphone apps on it like you can with Apple, but a lot of developers are opting to sunset their Apple Watch apps so no loss there.

I've had the watch since Sunday, fully charged and enabled all of the 24/7 features I need and the ETA on battery life is giving me 12 days which is outstanding. I've got no doubt in my mind that I can slap this watch on its charger once a week while I shower and I'll never have to worry about charging it daily.

I opted for the Ceramic model because the white looks sleek and modern. It matches the OLED display great. Everything is vibrant and clear.

My biggest gripe with this watch is that an app I use only supports Apple Watch as a way to count steps meaning I'm stuck carrying my phone around with me on workouts. I've given this watch 5 stars still because this is the apps fault, not Xiaomi's

Overall an outstanding watch and I absolutely love it. I don't see myself using a different watch/fitness tracker any time soon!

Uso il Redmi Watch 4 da dicembre e sono davvero soddisfatto dell’acquisto. L’ho scelto dopo un’attenta valutazione, e posso dire con certezza che in questa fascia di prezzo non ha rivali.

Le funzioni che utilizzo di più sono l’orologio, le chiamate (si collegano anche i contatti sull’iPhone senza problemi), il contapassi e le attività sportive – lo porto anche durante le sessioni di hydrobike, ed è perfettamente resistente all’acqua.

La batteria ha un’ottima durata, anche con uso costante. Il display AMOLED è brillante, con colori perfetti e visibilità eccellente anche sotto la luce diretta del sole.

Nonostante le dimensioni generose, è molto comodo al polso e non infastidisce nemmeno con un uso prolungato. Nessun problema di connessione con l’iPhone, anzi: è più reattivo di tanti altri smartwatch che ho provato.

Per me è il miglior smartwatch qualità-prezzo attualmente in commercio. Non ha nulla da invidiare ad Apple Watch, se non il prezzo (molto più basso). Super consigliato!

text:
I love the size of screen!
I am vision impaired & even though I adored my MiBand 7, it got more & more difficult for me to see to navigate the screen itself.
I wanted to love this just for the battery life alone, which is awesome compared to the 12-36 hours I've gotten from my fancier than needed, wanted or appreciated big screen, smartwatch that I used long enough to be annoyed and cheered when it developed an overheating problem, so I no longer had to guilt myself into using it :D...
This is comfortable to wear & didn't trigger any skin irritation (often an issue for me).
Regrettably I am sending this one back because for me a lack of Imperial measurements: feet inches miles and pounds is poor functionality, & in something I would be using to address some of my own accessibility needs, not having that available is a deal breaker :(
I so do NOT want to spend way too many minutes... hours staring at my watch trying to remember what the conversion rates are for kg & cm. By the time I get to a screen big enough to read giant fonts as paragraphs, with a real keyboard (giant font keycaps) to ask those questions, I have lost whatever enthusiasm motivation & impetus I had :(

I've submitted a question re: Xiaomi Smart Band 9 Pro Smartband Global Version, to find out if that model's "Global Version" includes Imperial measurements or if it's the change from the ZeppLife App which was consistently user friendly to the MiFitness App which apparently has less features?

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I bought this to replace my Galaxy Watch 5 (and a pink one to replace my girlfriend's Galaxy Watch 4), because we had to charge our watches every 14 hours or so and they were getting more sluggish by the month. I always like to break electronics down on a simple pros & cons list, so let's have at it (in alphabetical order).

_:PROS:_
- Battery life is superb. I could definitely see getting 3 weeks out of a charge if I turned off all the extra features. As it stands, I typically get at least 10 days with sleep tracking and AOD (always-on-display) turned on, (both of which the watch warns you will reduce battery life). Charging from ~10% to 100 only takes about 2 hours as well on a normal 1A charger.
--- Battery optimization options also are excellent, such as "smart AOD" (turns the screen off when the watch detects you're sleeping or when the watch isn't on your wrist at all). They can easily be found in Settings (gear icon)->Battery or Display.
- Exercise tracking has become very accurate after only TWO treadmill walks. There is an option at the end of walking or treadmill workouts to calibrate the distance traveled.
--- I did not realize this until AFTER my first treadmill walk, so I set my next distance walk to 2.2 mi, which is VERY close to 3.22 km.
----- It was over by about 200 meters, so I adjusted it to 3.22 and then my 3rd treadmill walk was within 0.01 km of my actual distance traveled, according to the treadmill, so I was very impressed by that.
- Notifications come through quickly from your default apps (messages, phone calls, email) as well as any other app that can send notifications to your phone, like games, security camera apps, etc.
--- Although pictures will not be displayed (MMS messages), texts with emojis do work.
--- You cannot answer calls from the watch, but you can mute or reject them as caller ID does pop up.
--- There is an option in the settings to deactivate notifications while your phone screen is unlocked, which is nice so you're not getting them in two places at once.
- Screen and overall user interface is very responsive - I was slightly uneasy about buying a watch with no buttons at all, but the screen feels incredibly reliable.
--- Also, there are a TON of different displays to switch to, simple Analog & Digital ones, as well as ones with more information and customizable ones into which you can insert pictures. This all feels great.
- Size & Design are very appealing - the screen does not feel too large even for my girlfriend - it is the perfect size.
- Sleep tracking with heart rate monitoring & REM tracking also feels pretty accurate. There is also an option to monitor night-time breathing rate, but that consumes more battery so I have not checked that off yet.

_:CONS:_
- Firstly, as it goes with many electronics and apps, it feels like you are signing your life and naming rights of your firstborn child away upon setup, but there is an easy-to-find option in the section "Profile->About this app" to "Revoke Authorization" if you change your mind on how much data is collected.
- Alarm app only allows you to "snooze" one time, then the alarm will not go off again until the next day, so you may need to set multiple alarms if you sleep through your first one, like I often do.
- I cannot find out how to change the distance units from the default km; you are able to change the weather units from C to F, but I have not yet found the option to toggle km to miles if it exists.
- Hiking & Walking programs: I do not believe there is a difference between these at all; this is not so much of a complaint, but on my older GPS-tracking watches, both programs would track your route. In addition, Hiking would also include changes in altitude, which I very much liked. So color me slightly disappointed to find, at the end of my hike, hills had not been accounted for. Again, minor thing overall, but that would have been nice to be included in the workout summary.

_:NEUTRALS:_
- In regards to the app, it is overall easy to use and find things.
- One odd thing is that the "Workout" section only contains 5 icon at the top (Outdoor running, Walking, Outdoor cycling, Treadmill & Jump Rope), but there are a TON more on the actual watch for other activities (aerobic / weight-training / swimming / etc.), just as a FYI...
- (not the company's fault) but aftermarket it definitely lighter for bands than other mainstream smartwatches - I've gotten a couple cool magnetic claps ones around the $10 - $15 mark that are well worth it though.

OVERALL, for under a hundred bucks, this definitely feels like the best tracker out there in terms of functionality, battery life, and usefulness. I consider myself pretty critical and my caveats are not even impactful enough to remove a star. Also, my girlfriend still raves about hers as well, so she still loves it and hasn't mentioned any of her own cons to me (and I have asked...).

text:
Après la panne de mon Apple Watch, j’ai choisi le Xiaomi Smart Band 9 Pro comme solution de remplacement, et je dois reconnaître que l’expérience est très positive. Le premier point marquant est l’autonomie : elle est réellement excellente. Avec une utilisation quotidienne (notifications, suivi du sommeil, activité physique), la montre tient plusieurs jours sans difficulté, ce qui change radicalement du rechargement quotidien d’une Apple Watch.

Au poignet, elle est extrêmement légère. On l’oublie complètement, même la nuit pour le suivi du sommeil. L’écran est large, lumineux et agréable à consulter, avec des bords très fins qui apportent une bonne immersion. Le prix est un autre point fort : pour cette gamme, l’offre est très attractive et permet d’accéder à une montre complète sans se ruiner.

Côté fonctionnalités, la montre reste efficace : plus de 150 modes sportifs, un suivi du sommeil précis et des notifications réactives. Le GPS intégré est correct pour un produit de cette catégorie.

En revanche, il faut être honnête : ce n’est pas une Apple Watch. Les capteurs sont moins nombreux, les mesures un peu moins poussées et l’écosystème Apple n’a pas d’équivalent ici. Mais au vu de la différence de prix, c’est totalement logique. Et surtout, les performances restent plus que suffisantes pour un usage quotidien classique.

En résumé, une excellente montre connectée : très légère, très autonome, agréable à utiliser et proposée à un prix imbattable. Un choix parfaitement cohérent si l’on cherche une alternative simple et fiable sans viser les fonctionnalités avancées d’une Apple Watch.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I'm a fan of the Xiaomi Smart Band. I used the Mi Band 5 and 7, and this time I bought the Mi Band 9. The app isn’t very intuitive, and the user guide for the Mi Band isn’t exactly easy to follow either. However, once I get used to the functions I want to use, the simplicity and lightweight comfort of the Mi Band make it the only one I end up using. The Mi Band 7 and 9 don’t seem to have changed much, but the 7 has been a great help to me over the past two years. The Mi Band 7 didn’t just stop working; it 'died in the line of duty,' having served me faithfully for two years before it passed away.

I’ll tell you the story of how I first got introduced to the Mi Band. Back then, it was the Mi Band 5, but since the difference in features is not significant compared to the current Mi Band 9, it remains a useful reference before making a purchase.

Company C’s warehouse somewhere in Asia—I worked 8 hours a day pulling a cart non-stop—literally no (official) break time. My job was to find the ordered items, load them up, and deliver them to the ladies who did the packing. The only time I could sit without worrying was during lunch. But being exhausted, full from eating, and sitting down? That’s a perfect recipe for dozing off every time. So, I decided to get myself a reliable alarm clock to keep me awake.

I considered a $2 stopwatch from a dollar store (Daiso), but it got eliminated in the final round because changing the battery was a hassle. Instead, I ended up with a much pricier but fancier Mi Band 5. On the first day, I was just happy it told time accurately, but then I realized—it also counted my heartbeats while I was dozing off. Wow, new tech. But, seriously, why? At this point, it might as well have had a feature that automatically alerts a funeral home if my heart stops while I’m sleeping. Anyway, back to work I went.

Here are my thoughts after using it for a few days—just personal impressions and some random questions. If you are already reading reviews, you probably know all the functions. So instead of a spec rundown, here’s how I actually use them:

Sleep Monitoring
It sends something—electrical signals? Radio waves?—to my wrist at intervals I set (once every minute or every 10 minutes). The fact that only my wrist feels sore in the morning tells me I have clearly been in an inappropriate relationship with this gadget overnight. I don’t even use a microwave, and this doesn’t feel great. But it’s fascinating, so I give it two nights. Then it starts nagging me like my mom did 30 years ago: "You went to bed too late. Sleep earlier. You didn’t get enough deep sleep." It even logs the exact time I get up to use the bathroom. Now, that’s impressive.

Exercise
The only workout I do is running. I don’t have any heart conditions, so I never care about heart rate. But I do like that it tracks my distance. At my age, I need to brag about how far I can still run.

Menstrual Cycle Tracking & Alerts
I’m a guy.

Battery Life & Charging
The battery lasts forever. Charging is easy. No complaints.

Stress Monitoring
I already know when I’m stressed. Do I really need a watch to tell me? Also, it doesn’t seem to differentiate between stress, tension, and excitement—like the kind of excitement you get from certain situations, for example.

Final Thoughts
If you are old enough to need reading glasses to see this text, listen up: Mi Band 9’s font is tiny. If you just want the time displayed in big numbers, that’s fine, but cramming multiple bits of info on one screen? Forget it.

It is packed with features, but let’s be real—who is actually going to check their sleep data every day for a year? Your sleep quality won’t improve just because you look at the numbers. And honestly, how many buyers really have serious arrhythmia concerns? Unless you do, heart rate tracking isn’t that useful. Also, if your phone is within reach, why would you squint at this tiny screen for texts or fumble with your fat fingers trying to change songs? That’s just comedy.

It is basically a cute gadget watch. But!

If you’ve read this far, you’re already too invested. Let’s be real—you’ll probably hit that "Buy Now" button tonight and go to bed pretending it never happened. Just get this over with, and stop thinking about your next purchase for now. Free yourself from the agony—buy it now, and move on.

Objectively, just the watch and step tracker alone make it worth it. It also has a handy feature to help you find your phone. A solid, sleek, and not-too-cheap-looking digital watch for under $45? That’s not easy to find. And if playing around with its features makes you enjoy working out for a month or two, that alone justifies the price. For serious fitness folks, you might even discover more useful functions than I did.

And when you get bored? Swap out the band (about $7) or trade it with your nephew for an Attack on Titan figurine, a popular anime character. It has a design that kids totally fall for.

Good luck.

text:
I had the Smart Band 6 previously, and when that one eventually died, I was happy to get the latest one, which was at the time, the Smart Band 9. Mostly I really like it. I keep my phone on silent, so the only feature that I really need is to be notified of incoming calls and texts. Everything else is nice to have, so spending $200, $400 or more for an Apple Watch is overkill when this one is $47 and does what I need.

Things I like:
- Durability
- Water resistant: I accidentally wore it in the shower a few times, and it was fine.
- Watch face is not huge like most smart watches.
- Color screen with lots of free watch faces.
- Syncs fine with iPhone.
- Long battery life.
- Value, as discussed above.

Cons:
- One other SUPER useful feature the Smart Band 6 had was that you could use the watch to make your phone beep so you could find it. While this one technically has that feature, there is one critical flaw: If my phone has its ringer off (again, see above - my phone is ALWAYS on silent), then when you use the watch to find the phone, it no longer beeps, it just vibrates. And this is not due to a change on Apple's side since I was using the same phone.
- A few of the watch faces are customizable, where you can choose what info you want displayed (steps vs heart rate vs ...). I wish more of them were customizable. Also more watch faces with large print and simple designs for those of us who have bad eyes would be much appreciated.

Overall, I 100% recommend this watch. Just verify if it has all the features you need. If so, get it!

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This is the 4th generation of Mi Bands I've had, beginning with Mi Band 5. I didn't really like the size switch (I think they made it bigger in gen 8) - as I really liked the slim band that you hardly knew was there. But, I have to say this band feels awfully sleek. And I don't really notice it that much.

The band is really soft - they also appear to have made it a little thicker. As I did break 2 or 3 bands over the years, this is probably a good thing.

The auto brightness is an awesome new feature - it was always a pain to adjust the watch for different lighting. Overall the look and feel of the operating system is definitely improved. I assume the heart rate tracking is as stellar as ever - Mi Band has always excelled in that area, and been very close to Apple in terms of accuracy. There's a guy on youtube from Germany or Switzerland who has a great technical comparison of different heart rate trackers, and Xiaomi Mi Bands have always done really well there.

Sleep tracking has always been not quite as good - but still a lot better than most. For people like me who just want to know "hey how many hours did I get last night" this band will undoubtedly be pretty spot on. Deep diving on your REM, etc - it probably won't rival the top trackers.

The biggest problem with the Xiaomi ecosystem has always been how crappy their fitness app has been. I used a 3rd party app for a long time. But the newest incarnation of the Mi Fit app that goes with this watch appears to have finally gotten it right. The app sort of gets out of the way, and gives you what you need pretty quickly. It appears to sync well, and works with things like Strava and Apple Health.

I wish I could fine tune the watch OS a little more - and get rid of all the activities I don't do, and just have about 5 or 6. I don't really see a way to do that right now.

But overall this watch feels like a pretty decent upgrade from the previous bands, including 8.

Highly recommended - probably the best fitness tracker on the planet for the money.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I've been on the hunt for good lighting in my office at night and this light bar is the final touch. I'll go over a few things I really like about it and the experience I've had

Quality: As soon as I pulled the mount out the box the first thing I said was "wow this is heavy". You can tell it's quality material. It is made to fit on practically any monitor, and my curved wide screen is no exception. I think it even works better with curved monitors because it's less likely to reflect light off the monitor. Which leads me to my next point

Lighting: A desk light should be able to light your desk without reflecting the light back in your face and this does just that. I like how I could adjust the light bar to where I need it and it's not hurting my eyes. I did notice how dirty my monitor was after turning it on and I cleaned it right away. I haven't had any problems with it showing reflections or smudges since I first cleaned it.

Wirless remote: Probably my favorite feature. It is very easy to use and quite responsive. I wish the remote was a little heavier tho.. you can tell that the rotating part of the remote is hollow. I would have liked a more premium feel. But I would still take this over the BenQ remote because I don't have to wave my hand over it to turn it on. This remote is just ready to go always. I really like the different temperatures you can choose from. I chose the one I like most for my set up and I just leave it at that.

Cable: Cable management is the Bain of my existence. I refuse to let cables ruin my life and I was very worried about the cable that came with this. I don't have any extra usb's on my monitor to plug it into, so my best bet was plugging it into the smart powerstrip I have stuck to the bottom of my desk. To my surprise the cable was exactly as long I needed, which was kind of disappointing in a way. I kinda wish it was a tich longer so I could still move stuff around if I needed, but I can't complain. I could also buy a new cable if I wanted.

Something else to keep in mind: If you're looking to use a smart plug with this, the light turns on when it gets power no matter if it was turned off before hand. This could be good or bad depending on what you want to do with it. You could have your home assistant control it and just forget about the remote. I personally don't want to do that because I love the remote.

Overall: I definitely recommend getting this! It's less than half of the price of the BenQ model, does the same thing, and has a better remote. It lights up my desk very well and doesn't reflect any light off my monitor. 5 stars!

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
After a month of use I am ready to give it a simple review. As a lifelong gamer with eyes sensitive to ghosting I'm usually a harsh critic when it comes to most screens.

So when I say that this discount off-brand monitor blew my mind please know that this isn't an exaggeration. Yes I may have gotten lucky, but regardless the model sent to me is surpassing every expectation.

PROS:

Speed - The screen seems most comfortable at either 120hz or 200hz. It felt a little off at 165 but that may be my own eyes.

Setting overdrive to Off or Normal seems to give the best results along with the high refresh.

Color - HDR is pretty damn good on this thing. Not as good as some expensive oleds would be but still surprisingly good. Otherwise set the screen to Movie for the brightest and most vivid SDR colors.

Cons:

MPRT felt weird to me. Reverse ghosting weird. So just leave that off.

Wasn't too big a fan of the VRR but it definitely works fine. Just kinda mutes the colors a notch and feels like strobbing but that is probably just my eyes. My friends and wife have all said it looks great with VRR to them. I just keep it set to 200hz

Conclusion: For the money you cant beat this screen. Ive been using it with games both on my PC and also streaming with GeForce Now (which seems to lock to 120hz on it) and it works great either way.
